records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 94
records.text: And this Book which we have sent down is blessed, confirming that which was before it; and in order that thou mightest warn the mother-city and those who dwell round about it. They who believe in the next life will believe in It, and will keep strictly to their Prayers.

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 95
records.text: But is any more wicked than he who deviseth a lie of God, or saith, "I have had a revelation," when nothing was revealed to him?25 And who saith, "I can bring down a book like that which God hath sent down"? But couldst thou see when the ungodly are in the floods of death, and the angels reach forth their hands, saying, "Yield up your souls:-this day shall ye be recompensed with a humiliating punishment for your untrue sayings about God, and for proudly rejecting his signs!"

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 96
records.text: "And now are ye come back to us, alone, as we created you at first, and ye leave behind you the good things which we had given you, and we see not with you your intercessors whom ye regarded as the companions of God among you. There is a severance between you now, and those whom ye regarded as partners with God have deserted you."

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 97
records.text: Verily God causeth the grain and the date stone to put forth: He bringeth forth the living from the dead, and the dead from the living! This is God! Why, then, are ye turned aside from Him?

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 98
records.text: He causeth the dawn to appear, and hath ordained the night for rest, and the sun and the moon for computing time! The ordinance of the Mighty, the Wise!

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 99
records.text: And it is He who hath ordained the stars for you that ye may be guided thereby in the darknesses of the land and of the sea! clear have we made our signs to men of knowledge.

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 100
records.text: And it is He who hath produced you from one man, and hath provided for you an abode and resting-place!26 Clear have we made our signs for men of insight.

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 101
records.text: And it is He who sendeth down rain from Heaven: and we bring forth by it the buds of all the plants, and from them bring we forth the green foliage, and the close growing grain, and palm trees with sheaths of clustering dates, and gardens of grapes, and the olive and the pomegranate, like and unlike.27 Look ye on their fruits when they fruit and ripen. Truly herein are signs unto people who believe.

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 102
records.text: Yet have they assigned the Djinn to God as his associates, though He created them; and in their ignorance have they falsely ascribed to him sons and daughters. Glory be to Him! And high let Him be exalted above that which they attribute to Him!

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 103
records.text: Sole maker of the Heavens and of the Earth! how, when He hath no consort, should He have a son? He hath created everything, and He knoweth everything!

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 104
records.text: This is God your Lord. There is no God but He, the creator of all things: therefore worship Him alone;-and He watcheth over all things.

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 105
records.text: No vision taketh in Him, but He taketh in all vision:28 and He is the Subtile, the All-informed.

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 106
records.text: Now have proofs that may be seen, come to you from your Lord; whoso seeth them, the advantage will be his own: and whoso is blind to them, his own will be the loss: I am not made a keeper over you.

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 107
records.text: Thus variously do we apply our signs,29 that they may say, "Thou hast studied deep:" and that to people of understanding we may make them clear.

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 108
records.text: Follow thou that which hath been revealed to thee by thy Lord: there is no god but He! and withdraw from those who join other gods with Him.

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 109
records.text: Had God pleased, they had not joined other gods with Him: and we have not made thee keeper over them, neither art thou a guardian over them.

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 110
records.text: Revile not those whom they call on beside God,30 lest they, in their ignorance, despitefully revile Him. Thus have we planned out their actions for every people; then shall they return to their Lord, and He will declare to them what those actions have been.

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 111
records.text: With their most solemn oath have they sworn by God, that if a sign come unto them they will certainly believe it; SAY: Signs are in the power of God alone; and He teacheth you not thereby, only because when they were wrought, ye did not believe.31

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 112
records.text: And we will turn their hearts and their eyes away from the truth, because they did not believe therein at first, and we will leave them in their transgressions, wandering in perplexity.

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 113
records.text: And though we had sent down the angels to them, and the dead had spoken to them, and we had gathered all things about them in tribes, they had not believed, unless God had willed it! but most of them do not know it.

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 114
records.text: Thus have we given an enemy to every prophet Satans among men and among Djinn: tinsel discourses do they suggest the one to the other, in order to deceive: and had thy Lord willed it, they would not have done it. Therefore, leave them and their vain imaginings-

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 115
records.text: And let the hearts of those who believe not in the life to come incline thereto, and let them find their content in this, and let them gain what they are gaining.

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 116
records.text: What! shall I seek other judge than God, when it is He who hath sent down to you the distinguishing Book? They to whom we have given the Book know that it is sent down from thy Lord with truth. Be not thou then of those who doubt.

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 117
records.text: And the words of thy Lord are perfect in truth and in justice: none can change his words: He is the Hearing, Knowing.

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 118
records.text: But if thou obey most men in this land, from the path of God will they mislead thee: they follow but a conceit, and they are only liars.

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 119
records.text: Thy Lord! He best knoweth those who err from his path, and He knoweth the rightly guided.

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 120
records.text: Eat32 of that over which the name of God hath been pronounced, if ye believe in his signs.

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 121
records.text: And why eat ye not of that over which the name of God hath been pronounced, since He hath made plain to you what He hath forbidden you, save as to that which is forced upon you? But indeed many mislead others by their appetites, through lack of knowledge. Verily, thy Lord! He best knoweth the transgressors.

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 122
records.text: And abandon the semblance of wickedness, and wickedness itself.33 They, verily, whose only acquirement is iniquity, shall be rewarded for what they shall have gained.

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 123
records.text: Eat not therefore of that on which the name of God has not been named, for that is assuredly a crime: the Satans will indeed suggest to their votaries to wrangle with you; but if ye obey them, ye will indeed be of those who join gods with God.

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 124
records.text: Shall the dead, whom we have quickened, and for whom we have ordained a light whereby he may walk among men, be like him, whose likeness is in the darkness, whence he will not come forth? Thus have the doings of the unbelievers been prepared for them.

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 125
records.text: Even so have we placed in every city, ringleaders of its wicked ones, to scheme therein: but only against themselves shall they scheme! and they know it not.

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 126
records.text: And when a sign cometh to them they say, "We will not believe, till the like of what was accorded to the apostles of God, be accorded to us." God best knoweth where to place his mission. Disgrace with God, and a vehement punishment shall come on the transgressors for their crafty plottings.

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 127
records.text: And whom God shall please to guide, that man's breast will He open to Islam; but whom He shall please to mislead, strait and narrow will He make his breast, as though he were mounting up into the very Heavens! Thus doth God inflict dire punishment on those who believe not.

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 128
records.text: And this is the right way of thy Lord. Now have we detailed our signs unto those who will consider.

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 129
records.text: For them is a dwelling of peace with their Lord! and in recompense for their works, shall he be their protector.

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 130
records.text: On the day whereon God shall gather them all together . . . "O race of Djinn," will He say, "much did ye exact from mankind." And their votaries from among men shall say, "O our Lord! we rendered one another mutual services: but we have reached our set term, which thou hast set for us." He will say, "Your abode the fire! therein abide ye for ever: unless as God shall will." Verily, thy Lord is Wise, Knowing.

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 131
records.text: Even thus place we some of the wicked over others, as the meed of their doings.

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 132
records.text: O race of Djinn and men! came not apostles to you from among yourselves, rehearsing my signs to you, and warning you of the meeting of this your day? They shall say, "We bear witness against ourselves." This world's life deceived them; and they shall bear witness against themselves that they were infidels:-

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 133
records.text: This,34 because thy Lord would not destroy the cities in their sin, while their people were yet careless.

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 134
records.text: And for all, are grades of recompense as the result of their deeds; and of what they do, thy Lord is not regardless.

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 135
records.text: And thy Lord is the Rich one, full of compassion! He can destroy you if He please, and cause whom He will to succeed you, as he raised you up from the offspring of other people:

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 136
records.text: Verily, that which is threatened you shall surely come to pass, neither shall ye weaken its might.

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 137
records.text: SAY: O my people! Act as ye best can: I verily will act my part, and hereafter shall ye know

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 138
records.text: Whose will be the recompense of the abode! Verily, the ungodly shall not prosper.

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 139
records.text: Moreover, they set apart a portion of the fruits and cattle35 which he hath produced, and say, "This for God"-so deem they-"And this for his companions, whom we associate with Him." But that which is for these companions of theirs, cometh not to God; yet that which is for God, cometh to the companions! Ill do they judge.

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 140
records.text: Thus have the companion-gods induced many of these, who join them with God, to slay their children, that they might ruin them, and throw the cloak of confusion over their religion. But if God had pleased, they had not done this. Therefore, leave them and their devices.

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 141
records.text: They also say, "These cattle and fruits are sacred: none may taste them but whom we please:" so deem they-"And there are cattle, whose backs should be exempt from labour." And there are cattle over which they do not pronounce the name of God: inventing in all this a lie against Him. For their inventions shall He reward them.

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 142
records.text: And they say, "That which is in the wombs of these cattle is allowed to our males, and forbidden to our wives;" but if it prove abortive, both partake of it. God shall reward them for their distinctions! Knowing, Wise is He.

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 143
records.text: Lost are they who, in their ignorance, have foolishly slain their children, and have forbidden that which God hath given them for food, devising an untruth against God! Now have they erred; and they were not rightly guided.

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 144
records.text: He it is who produceth gardens of the vine trellised and untrellised, and the palm trees, and the corn of various food, and olives, and pomegranates, like and unlike. Eat of their fruit when they bear fruit, and pay the due thereof on the day of its ingathering: and be not prodigal, for God loveth not the prodigal.

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 145
records.text: And there are cattle for burdens and for journeys. Eat of what God hath given you for food; and follow not the steps of Satan, for he is your declared enemy.

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 146
records.text: You have four sorts of cattle in pairs: of sheep a pair, and of goats a pair. SAY: Hath He forbidden the two males or the two females; or that which the wombs of the two females enclose? Tell me with knowledge, if ye speak the truth:

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 147
records.text: And of camels a pair, and of oxen a pair. SAY: Hath He forbidden the two males or the two females; or that which the wombs of the two females enclose?36 Were ye witnesses when God enjoined you this? Who then is more wicked than he who, in his ignorance, inventeth a lie against God, to mislead men? God truly guideth not the wicked.

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 148
records.text: SAY: I find not in what hath been revealed to me aught forbidden to the eater to eat, except it be that which dieth of itself, or blood poured forth, or swine's flesh; for this is unclean or profane, being slain in the name of other than God. But whoso shall be a forced partaker, if it be without wilfulness, and not in transgression,-verily, thy Lord is Indulgent, Merciful!

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 149
records.text: To the Jews did we forbid every beast having an entire hoof, and of both bullocks and sheep we forbade them the fat, save what might be on their backs, or their entrails, and the fat attached to the bone. With this have we recompensed them, because of their transgression: and verily, we are indeed equitable.

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 150
records.text: If they treat thee as an impostor, then SAY: Your Lord is of all-embracing mercy: but his severity shall not be turned aside from the wicked.

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 151
records.text: They who add gods to God will say, "If God had pleased, neither we nor our fathers had given him companions, nor should we have interdicted anything." Thus did they who flourished before them charge with imposture, until they had tasted our severity! SAY: Have ye any knowledge that ye can produce to us? Verily, ye follow only a conceit: ye utter only lies!

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 152
records.text: SAY: Peremptory proof is God's! Had He pleased He had guided you all aright.

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 153
records.text: SAY: Bring hither your witnesses who can witness that God hath forbidden these animals; but if they bear witness, witness not thou with them, nor witness to the conceits of those who charge our signs with falsehood, and who believe not in the life to come, and give equals to our Lord.

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 154
records.text: SAY: Come, I will rehearse what your Lord hath made binding on you-that ye assign not aught to Him as partner; and that ye be good to your parents; and that ye slay not your children, because of poverty: for them and for you will we provide:37 and that ye come not near to pollutions, outward or inward:38 and that ye slay not anyone whom God hath forbidden you, unless for a just cause. This hath he enjoined on you, to the intent that ye may understand.

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 155
records.text: And come not nigh to the substance of the orphan, but to improve it, until he come of age: and use a full measure, and a just balance: We will not task a soul beyond its ability. And when ye give judgment, observe justice, even though it be the affair of a kinsman, and fulfil the covenant of God. This hath God enjoined you for your monition-

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 156
records.text: And, "this is my right way." Follow it then; and follow not other paths lest ye be scattered from His path. This hath he enjoined you, that ye may fear Him.

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 157
records.text: Then39 gave we the Book to Moses-complete for him who should do right, and a decision for all matters, and a guidance, and a mercy, that they might believe in the meeting with their Lord.

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 158
records.text: Blessed, too, this Book which we have sent down. Wherefore follow it and fear God, that ye may find mercy:

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 159
records.text: Lest ye should say, "The Scriptures were indeed sent down only unto two peoples before us, but we were not able to go deep into their studies:"40

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 160
records.text: Or lest ye should say, "If a book had been sent down to us, we had surely followed the guidance better than they." But now hath a clear exposition come to you from your Lord, and a guidance and a mercy. Who then is more wicked than he who treateth the signs of God as lies, and turneth aside from them? We will recompense those who turn aside from our signs with an evil punishment, because they have turned aside.

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 161
records.text: What wait they for, but the coming of the angels to them, or the coming of thy Lord Himself, or that some of the sings of the Lord should come to pass? On the day when some of thy Lord's signs shall come to pass, its faith shall not profit a soul which believed not before, nor wrought good works in virtue of its faith. SAY: Wait ye. Verily, we will wait also.

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 162
records.text: As to those who split up their religion and become sects, have thou nothing to do with them: their affair is with God only. Hereafter shall he tell them what they have done.

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 163
records.text: He who shall present himself with good works shall receive a tenfold reward; but he who shall present himself with evil works shall receive none other than a like punishment: and they shall not be treated unjustly.

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 164
records.text: SAY: As for me, my Lord hath guided me into a straight path; a true religion, the creed of Abraham, the sound in faith; for he was not of those who join gods with God.

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 165
records.text: SAY: My prayers and my worship and my life and my death are unto God, Lord of the Worlds. He hath no associate. This am I commanded, and I am the first of the Muslims.

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 166
records.text: SAY: Shall I seek any other Lord than God, when He is Lord of all things? No soul shall labour but for itself; and no burdened one shall bear another's burden. At last ye shall return to your Lord, and he will declare that to you about which you differ.

records.label: Surah 6 · edition paragraph 167
records.text: And it is He who hath made you the successors of others on the earth, and hath raised some of you above others by various grades, that he may prove you by his gifts. Verily thy Lord is swift to punish. But He is also Gracious, Merciful!

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 1
records.text: In the Name of God, the Compassionate, the Merciful

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 2
records.text: ELIF. LAM. MIM. SAD.1 A Book hath been sent down to thee: therefore let there be no difficulty in thy breast concerning it: to the intent that thou mayest warn thereby, and that it may be a monition to the faithful.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 3
records.text: Follow ye what hath been sent down to you from your Lord; and follow no masters beside Him. How little will ye be monished!

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 4
records.text: How many cities have we destroyed! By night, or while they were in their midday slumber, did our wrath reach them!

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 5
records.text: And what was their cry when our wrath reached them, but to say, "Verily, we have been impious."

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 6
records.text: Surely, therefore, will we call those to account, to whom an Apostle hath been sent, and of the sent ones themselves will we certainly demand a reckoning.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 7
records.text: And with knowledge will we tell them of their deeds, for we were not absent from them.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 8
records.text: The weighing2 on that day, with justice! and they whose balances shall be heavy, these are they who shall be happy.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 9
records.text: And they whose balances shall be light, these are they who have lost their souls, for that to our signs they were unjust:

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 10
records.text: And now have we stabilished you on the earth, and given you therein the supports of life. How little do ye give thanks!

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 11
records.text: We created you; then fashioned you; then said we to the angels, "Prostrate yourselves unto Adam: and they prostrated them all in worship, save Eblis: He was not among those who prostrated themselves.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 12
records.text: To him said God: "What hath hindered thee from prostrating thyself in worship at my bidding?" He said, "Nobler am I than he: me hast thou created of fire; of clay hast thou created him."

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 13
records.text: He said, "Get thee down hence: Paradise is no place for thy pride: Get thee gone then; one of the despised shalt thou be."

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 14
records.text: He said, "Respite me till the day when mankind shall be raised from the dead."

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 15
records.text: He said, "One of the respited shalt thou be."

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 16
records.text: He said, "Now, for that thou hast caused me to err, surely in thy straight path will I lay wait for them:

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 17
records.text: Then will I surely come upon them from before, and from behind, and from their right hand, and from their left, and thou shalt not find the greater part of them to be thankful."

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 18
records.text: He said, "Go forth from it, a scorned, a banished one! Whoever of them shall follow thee, I will surely fill hell with you, one and all.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 19
records.text: And, O Adam! dwell thou and thy wife in Paradise, and eat ye whence ye will, but to this tree approach not, lest ye become of the unjust doers."

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 20
records.text: Then Satan whispered them to shew them their nakedness, which had been hidden from them both. And he said, "This tree3 hath your Lord forbidden you, only lest ye should become angels, or lest ye should become immortals."

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 21
records.text: And he sware to them both, "Verily I am unto you one who counselleth aright."

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 22
records.text: So he beguiled them by deceits: and when they had tasted of the tree, their nakedness appeared to them, and they began to sew together upon themselves the leaves of the garden. And their Lord called to them, "Did I not forbid you this tree, and did I not say to you, 'Verily, Satan is your declared enemy.' "

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 23
records.text: They said, "O our Lord! With ourselves have we dealt unjustly: if thou forgive us not and have pity on us, we shall surely be of those who perish."

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 24
records.text: He said, "Get ye down, the one of you an enemy4 to the other; and on earth shall be your dwelling, and your provision for a season."

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 25
records.text: He said, "On it shall ye live, and on it shall ye die, and from it shall ye be taken forth."

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 26
records.text: O children of Adam! now have we sent down to you raiment to hide your nakedness, and splendid garments; but the raiment of piety-this is best. This is one of the signs of God, that man haply may reflect.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 27
records.text: O children of Adam! let not Satan bring you into trouble, as he drove forth your parents from the Garden, by despoiling them of their raiment, that he might cause them to see their nakedness: He truly seeth you, he and his comrades, whence ye see not them. Verily, we have made the Satans tutelars of those who believe not.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 28
records.text: And when the wicked commit some filthy deed, they say, "We found our fathers practising it, and to us hath God commanded it"-SAY: God enjoineth not filthy deeds. Will ye speak of God ye know not what?

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 29
records.text: SAY: My Lord hath enjoined what is right. Turn your faces therefore towards every place where he is worshipped5 and call upon him with sincere religion. As he created you, to him shall ye return: some hath he guided, and some hath he justly left in error, because they have taken the Satans as their tutelars beside God, and have deemed that they were guided aright.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 30
records.text: O children of Adam! wear your goodly apparel when ye repair to any mosque,6 and eat ye and drink; but exceed not, for He loveth not those who exceed.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 31
records.text: SAY: Who hath prohibited God's goodly raiment, and the healthful viands which He hath provided for his servants? SAY: These are for the faithful in this present life, but above all on the day of the resurrection. Thus make we our signs plain for people of knowledge.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 32
records.text: SAY: Truly my Lord hath forbidden filthy actions whether open or secret, and iniquity, and unjust violence, and to associate with God that for which He hath sent down no warranty, and to speak of God that ye know not.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 33
records.text: Every nation hath its set time. And when their time is come, they shall not retard it an hour; and they shall not advance it.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 34
records.text: O children of Adam! there shall come to you Apostles from among yourselves, rehearsing my signs to you; and whoso shall fear God and do good works, no fear shall be upon them, neither shall they be put to grief.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 35
records.text: But they who charge our signs with falsehood, and turn away from them in their pride, shall be inmates of the fire: for ever shall they abide therein.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 36
records.text: And who is worse than he who deviseth a lie of God, or treateth our signs as lies? To them shall a portion here below be assigned in accordance with the Book of our decrees, until the time when our messengers,7 as they receive their souls, shall say, "Where are they on whom ye called beside God?" They shall say: "Gone from us." And they shall witness against themselves that they were infidels.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 37
records.text: He shall say, "Enter ye into the Fire with the generations of Djinn and men who have preceded you. So oft as a fresh generation entereth, it shall curse its sister, until when they have all reached it, the last comers shall say to the former, 'O our Lord! these are they who led us astray: assign them therefore a double torment of the fire:"' He will say, "Ye shall all have double." But of this are ye ignorant.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 38
records.text: And the former of them shall say to the latter, "What advantage have ye over us? Taste ye therefore the torment for that which ye have done."

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 39
records.text: Verily, they who have charged our signs with falsehood and have turned away from them in their pride, Heaven's gates shall not be opened to them, nor shall they enter Paradise, until the camel8 passeth through the eye of the needle. After this sort will we recompense the transgressors.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 40
records.text: They shall make their bed in Hell, and above them shall be coverings of fire! After this sort will we recompense the evil doers.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 41
records.text: But as to those who have believed and done the things which are right (we will lay on no one a burden beyond his power) These shall be inmates of Paradise: for ever shall they abide therein;

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 42
records.text: And we will remove whatever rancour was in their bosoms: rivers shall roll at their feet: and they shall say, "Praise be to God who hath guided us hither! We had not been guided had not God guided us! Of a surety the Apostles of our Lord came to us with truth." And a voice shall cry to them, "This is Paradise, of which, as the meed of your works, ye are made heirs."

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 43
records.text: And the inmates of Paradise shall cry to the inmates of the fire, "Now have we found what our Lord promised us to be true. Have ye too found what your Lord promised you to be true?" And they shall answer, "Yes." And a Herald shall proclaim between them: "The curse of God be upon the evil doers,

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 44
records.text: Who turn men aside from the way of God, and seek to make it crooked, and who believe not in the life to come!"

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 45
records.text: And between them shall be a partition; and on the wall AL ARAF9 shall be men who will know all,10 by their tokens, and they shall cry to the inmates of Paradise, "Peace be on you!" but they shall not yet enter it, although they long to do so.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 46
records.text: And when their eyes are turned towards the inmates of the Fire, they shall say, "O our Lord! place us not with the offending people."

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 47
records.text: And they who are upon Al Araf shall cry to those whom they shall know by their tokens, "Your amassings and your pride have availed you nothing.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 48
records.text: Are these they on whom ye sware God would not bestow mercy? Enter ye11 into Paradise! where no fear shall be upon you, neither shall ye be put to grief."

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 49
records.text: And the inmates of the fire shall cry to the inmates of Paradise: "Pour upon us some water, or of the refreshments12 God hath given you?" They shall say, "Truly God hath forbidden both to unbelievers,

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 50
records.text: Who made their religion a sport and pastime, and whom the life of the world hath deceived." This day therefore will we forget them, as they forgot the meeting of this their day, and as they did deny our signs.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 51
records.text: And now have we brought them the Book: with knowledge have we explained it; a guidance and a mercy to them that believe.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 52
records.text: What have they to wait for now but its interpretation? When its interpretation13 shall come, they who aforetime were oblivious of it shall say, "The Prophets of our Lord did indeed bring the truth; shall we have any intercessor to intercede for us? or could we not be sent back? Then would we act otherwise than we have acted." But they have ruined themselves; and the deities of their own devising have fled from them!

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 53
records.text: Your Lord is God, who in six days created the Heavens and the Earth, and then mounted the throne: He throweth the veil of night over the day: it pursueth it swiftly: and he created the sun and the moon and the stars, subjected to laws by His behest: Is not all creation and its empire His? Blessed be God the Lord of the Worlds!

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 54
records.text: Call upon your Lord with lowliness and in secret, for He loveth not transgressors.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 55
records.text: And commit not disorders on the earth after it hath been well ordered; and call on Him with fear and longing desire: Verily the mercy of God is nigh unto the righteous.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 56
records.text: And He it is who sendeth forth the winds as the heralds of his compassion,14 until they bring up the laden clouds, which we drive along to some dead land and send down water thereon, by which we cause an upgrowth of all kinds of fruit.-Thus will we bring forth the dead. Haply ye will reflect.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 57
records.text: In a rich soil, its plants spring forth abundantly by the will of its Lord, and in that which is bad, they spring forth but scantily. Thus do We diversify our signs for those who are thankful.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 58
records.text: Of old sent We Noah to his people,15 and he said, "O my people! worship God. Ye have no God but Him: indeed I fear for you the chastisement of the great day."

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 59
records.text: The chiefs of his people said, "We clearly see that thou art in a palpable error."

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 60
records.text: He said, "There is no error in me, O my people! but I am a messenger from the Lord of the Worlds.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 61
records.text: I bring to you the messages of my Lord, and I give you friendly counsel; for I know from God what ye know not.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 62
records.text: Marvel ye that a Warning should come to you from your Lord through one of yourselves, that he may warn you, and that ye may fear for yourselves, and that haply ye may find mercy?"

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 63
records.text: But they treated him as a liar: so we delivered him and those who were with him in the ark, and we drowned those who charged our signs with falsehood; for they were a blind people.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 64
records.text: And to Ad16 we sent their brother Houd.17 "O my people!" said he, "worship God: ye have no other god than Him: Will ye not then fear Him?"

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 65
records.text: Said the unbelieving chiefs among his people, "We certainly perceive that thou art unsound of mind; and we surely deem thee an impostor."

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 66
records.text: He said, "O my people! it is not unsoundness of mind in me, but I am an Apostle from the Lord of the Worlds.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 67
records.text: The messages of my Lord do I announce to you, and I am your faithful18 counsellor.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 68
records.text: Marvel ye that a warning hath come to you from your Lord through one of yourselves that He may warn you? Remember how he hath made you the successors of the people of Noah, and increased you in tallness of stature. Remember then the favours of God, that it may haply be well with you."

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 69
records.text: They said, "Art thou come to us in order that we may worship one God alone, and leave what our fathers worshipped? Then bring that upon us with which thou threatenest us, if thou be a man of truth."

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 70
records.text: He said, "Vengeance and wrath shall suddenly light on you from your Lord. Do ye dispute with me about names that you and your fathers have given your idols, and for which God hath sent you down no warranty? Wait ye then, and I too will wait with you."

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 71
records.text: And we delivered him, and those who were on his side, by our mercy, and we cut off, to the last man, those who had treated our signs as lies, and who were not believers.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 72
records.text: And to Themoud we sent their brother Saleh.19 He said, O my people! worship God: ye have no other god than Him: now hath a clear proof of my mission come to you from your Lord, this she-camel of God being a sign to you: therefore let her go at large to pasture on God's earth: and touch her not to harm her, lest a grievous chastisement seize you.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 73
records.text: And remember how he hath made you successors to the Adites, and given you dwellings on the earth, so that on its plains ye build castles, and hew out houses in the hills. And bear in mind the benefits of God, and lay not the earth waste with deeds of licence.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 74
records.text: Said the chiefs of his people puffed up with pride, to those who were esteemed weak, even to those of them who believed, "What! know ye for certain that Saleh is sent by his Lord?" They said, "Truly we believe in that with which he hath been sent."

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 75
records.text: Then said those proud men, "Verily, we reject that in which ye believe."

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 76
records.text: And they ham-strung the she-camel, and rebelled against their Lord's command, and said, "O Saleh, let thy menaces be accomplished upon us if thou art one of the Sent Ones."

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 77
records.text: Then the earthquake surprised them; and in the morning they were found dead on their faces in their dwellings.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 78
records.text: So he turned away from them, and said, "O my people! I did indeed announce to you the message of my Lord: and I gave you faithful counsel, but ye love not faithful counsellors.20

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 79
records.text: We also sent Lot, when he said to his people, commit ye this filthy deed in which no creature hath gone before you?

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 80
records.text: Come ye to men, instead of women, lustfully? Ye are indeed a people given up to excess.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 81
records.text: But the only answer of his people was to say, "Turn them out of your city, for they are men who vaunt them pure."

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 82
records.text: And we delivered him and his family, except his wife; she was of those who lingered:

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 83
records.text: And we rained a rain upon them: and see what was the end of the wicked!

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 84
records.text: And we sent to Madian21 their brother Shoaib. He said, "O my people! worship God; ye have no other God than Him: now hath a clear sign come to you from your Lord: give therefore the full in measures and weights; take from no man his chattels, and commit no disorder on the earth after it has been made so good. This will be better for you, if you will believe it.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 85
records.text: And lay not in ambush by every road in menacing sort; nor mislead him who believeth in God, from His way, nor seek to make it crooked; and remember when ye were few and that he multiplied you, and behold what hath been the end of the authors of disorder!

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 86
records.text: And if a part of you believe in that with which I am sent, and a part of you believe not, then wait steadfastly until God shall judge between us, for He is the best of judges."

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 87
records.text: Said the chiefs of his people puffed up with pride, "We will surely banish thee, O Shoaib, and thy fellow-believers from our cities, unless indeed ye shall come back to our religion." "What!" said he, "though we abhor it?

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 88
records.text: Now shall we have devised a lie concerning God, if after he hath delivered us from your religion we shall return to it; nor can we return to it, unless by the will of God our Lord: our Lord embraceth all things in his ken. In God have we put our trust: O our Lord! decide between us and between our people, with truth; for the best to decide art Thou."

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 89
records.text: And the chiefs of his people who believed not, said, "If ye follow Shoaib, ye shall then surely perish."

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 90
records.text: An earthquake therefore surprised them, and they were found in the morning dead on their faces, in their dwellings.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 91
records.text: Those who had treated Shoaib as an impostor, became as though they had never dwelt in them: they who treated Shoaib as an impostor, were they that perished.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 92
records.text: So he turned away from them and said, O my people! I proclaimed to you the messages of my Lord, and I counselled you aright; but how should I be grieved for a people who do not believe?

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 93
records.text: Nor did we ever send a prophet to any city without afflicting its people with adversity and trouble, that haply they might humble them.22

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 94
records.text: Then changed we their ill for good, until they waxed wealthy, and said, "Of old did troubles and blessings befall our fathers:" therefore did we seize upon them suddenly when they were unaware.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 95
records.text: But if that the people of these cities had believed and feared us, we would surely have laid open to them blessings out of the Heaven and the Earth: but they treated our signs as lies, and we took vengeance on them for their deeds.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 96
records.text: Were the people, therefore, of those cities secure that our wrath would not light on them by night, while they were slumbering?

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 97
records.text: Were the people of those cities secure that our wrath would not light on them in broad day, while they were disporting themselves?

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 98
records.text: Did they, therefore, deem themselves secure from the deep counsel23 of God? But none deem themselves secure from the deep counsel of God, save those who perish.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 99
records.text: Is it not proved to those who inherit this land after its ancient occupants, that if we please we can smite them for their sins, and put a seal upon their hearts, that they hearken not?

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 100
records.text: We will tell thee the stories of these cities. Their apostles came to them with clear proofs of their mission; but they would not believe in what they had before treated as imposture.-Thus doth God seal up the hearts of the unbelievers-

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 101
records.text: And we found not of their covenant in most of them; but we found most of them to be perverse.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 102
records.text: Then after them we sent Moses with our signs to Pharaoh and his nobles, who acted unjustly in their regard. But see what was the end of the corrupt doers!

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 103
records.text: And Moses said, "O Pharaoh! verily I am an apostle from the Lord of the Worlds.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 104
records.text: Nothing but truth is it right for me to speak of God. Now am I come to you from your Lord with a proof of my mission; send away, therefore, the children of Israel with me." He said, "If thou comest with a sign, shew it if thou art a man of truth."

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 105
records.text: So he threw down his rod, and lo! it distinctly became a serpent.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 106
records.text: Then drew he forth his hand, and lo! it was white24 to the beholders.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 107
records.text: The nobles of Pharaoh's people said, "Verily, this is an expert enchanter:

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 108
records.text: Fain would he expel you from your land: what then do ye order to be done?"

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 109
records.text: They said, "Put25 him and his brother off awhile, and send round men to your cities who shall muster

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 110
records.text: And bring to thee every skilled enchanter."

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 111
records.text: And the enchanters came to Pharaoh. Said they, "Shall we surely be rewarded if we prevail?"

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 112
records.text: He said, "Yes; and ye certainly shall be near my person."

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 113
records.text: They said, "O Moses! either cast thou down thy rod first, or we will cast down ours."

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 114
records.text: He said, "Cast ye down." And when they had cast them down they enchanted the people's eyes, and made them afraid; for they had displayed a great enchantment.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 115
records.text: Then spake we unto Moses, "Throw down thy rod;" and lo! it devoured their lying wonders.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 116
records.text: So the truth was made strong, and that which they had wrought proved vain:

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 117
records.text: And they were vanquished on the spot, and drew back humiliated.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 118
records.text: But the other enchanters prostrated themselves adoring:

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 119
records.text: Said they, "We believe on the Lord of the Worlds,

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 120
records.text: The Lord of Moses and Aaron."

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 121
records.text: Said Pharaoh, "Have ye believed on him, ere I have given you leave? This truly is a plot which ye have plotted in this my city, in order to drive out its people. But ye shall see in the end what shall happen.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 122
records.text: I will surely cut off your hands and feet on opposite sides; then will I have you all crucified."

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 123
records.text: They said, "Verily, to our Lord do we return;

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 124
records.text: And thou takest vengeance on us only because we have believed on the signs of our Lord when they came to us. Lord! pour out constancy upon us, and cause us to die Muslims."

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 125
records.text: Then said the chiefs of Pharaoh's people-"Wilt thou let Moses and his people go to spread disorders in our land, and desert thee and thy gods?" He said, "We will cause their male children to be slain and preserve their females alive: and verily we shall be masters over them."

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 126
records.text: Said Moses to his people, "Cry unto God for help, and bear up patiently, for the earth is God's: to such of His servants as He pleaseth doth He give it as a heritage; and for those that fear Him is a happy issue."

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 127
records.text: "We have been oppressed," they said, "before thou camest to us, and since thou hast been with us:" "Perhaps," said he, "your Lord will destroy your enemy, and will make you his successors in the land, and He will see how ye will act therein."

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 128
records.text: Already had we chastised the people of Pharaoh with dearth and scarcity of fruits, that haply they might take warning:

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 129
records.text: And when good fell to their lot they said, "This is our due." But if ill befel them, they regarded Moses and his partisans as (the birds) of evil omen.26 Yet, was not their evil omen from God? But most of them knew it not.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 130
records.text: And they said, "Whatever sign thou bring us for our enchantment, we will not believe on thee."

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 131
records.text: And we sent upon them the flood and the locusts and the kummal (lice) and the frogs and the blood,-clear signs27-but they behaved proudly, and were a sinful people.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 132
records.text: And when any plague fell upon them, they said, "O Moses! pray for us to thy Lord, according to that which he hath covenanted with thee: Truly if thou take off the plague from us, we will surely believe thee, and will surely send the children of Israel with thee." But when we had taken off the plague from them, and the time which God had granted them had expired,28 behold! they broke their promise.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 133
records.text: Therefore we took vengeance on them and drowned them in the sea, because they treated our signs as falsehoods and were heedless of them.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 134
records.text: And we gave to the people who had been brought so low, the eastern and the western lands, which we had blessed as an heritage: and the good word of thy Lord was fulfilled on the children of Israel because they had borne up with patience: and we destroyed the works and the structures of Pharaoh and his people:

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 135
records.text: And we brought the children of Israel across the sea, and they came to a people who gave themselves up to their idols. They said, "O Moses! make us a god, as they have gods." He said, "Verily, ye are an ignorant people:

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 136
records.text: For the worship they practise29 will be destroyed, and that which they do, is vain."

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 137
records.text: He said, "Shall I seek any other god for you than God, when it is He who hath preferred you above all other peoples?"

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 138
records.text: And remember when we rescued you from the people of Pharaoh they had laid on you a cruel affliction; they slew your sons, and let only your daughters live, and in this was a great trial from your Lord.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 139
records.text: And we appointed a meeting with Moses for thirty nights, which we completed with ten other nights, so that his whole time with his Lord30 amounted to forty nights. Then said Moses to his brother Aaron, "Take thou my place among my people, and act rightly, and follow not the way of the corrupt doers."

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 140
records.text: And when Moses came at our set time and his Lord spake with him, he said, "O Lord, shew thyself to me, that I may look upon thee." He said, "Thou shalt not see Me; but look towards the mount, and if it abide firm in its place, then shalt thou see Me." And when God manifested Himself to the mountain he turned it to dust! and Moses fell in a swoon.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 141
records.text: And when he came to himself, he said, "Glory be to thee! To thee do I turn in penitence, and I am the first of them that believe."

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 142
records.text: He said, "O Moses! thee above all men have I chosen by my commissions, and by my speaking to thee. Take therefore what I have brought thee, and be one of those who render thanks.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 143
records.text: And we wrote for him upon the tables a monition concerning every matter, and said, "Receive them thyself with steadfastness, and command thy people to receive them for the observance of its most goodly precepts:-I will shew you the abode of the wicked."

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 144
records.text: The unjustly proud ones of the earth will I turn aside from my signs, for even if they see every sign they will not believe them; and if they see the path of uprightness, they will not take it for their path, but if they see the path of error, for their path will they take it.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 145
records.text: This,-for that they treated our signs as lies, and were heedless of them.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 146
records.text: Vain will be the works of those who treated our signs, and the meeting of the life to come, as lies! Shall they be rewarded but as they have wrought?

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 147
records.text: And the people of Moses took during his absence a calf made of their ornaments, and ruddy like gold, and lowing.31 Saw they not that it could not speak to them, nor guide them in the way?

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 148
records.text: Yet they took if for a God and became offenders!

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 149
records.text: But when they repented, and saw that they had erred, they said, Truly if our Lord have not mercy on us, and forgive us, we shall surely be of those who perish.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 150
records.text: And when Moses returned to his people, wrathful, angered, he said, "Evil is it that ye have done next upon my departure. Would ye hasten on the judgments of your Lord?" And he threw down the tables, and seized his brother by the head and dragged him unto him. Said he, "Son of my mother! the people thought me weak, and had well nigh slain me. Make not mine enemies to rejoice over me, and place me not among the wrong doers."

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 151
records.text: He said, "O Lord, forgive me and my brother, and bring us into thy mercy; for of those who shew mercy thou art the most merciful."

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 152
records.text: Verily as to those who took the calf as a god, wrath from their Lord shall overtake them, and shame in this present life: for thus recompense we the devisers of a lie.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 153
records.text: But to those who have done evil, then afterwards repent and believe, thy Lord will thereafter be Lenient, Merciful.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 154
records.text: And when the anger of Moses was stilled, he took up the tables; and in their writing was guidance and mercy for those who dread their Lord.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 155
records.text: And Moses chose seventy men of his people for a meeting appointed by us. And when the earthquake overtook them, he said, "O my Lord! if it had been thy pleasure, thou hadst destroyed them and me ere this! wilt thou destroy us for what our foolish ones have done? It is nought but thy trial: thou wilt mislead by it whom thou wilt, and guide whom thou wilt. Our guardian, thou! Forgive us then and have mercy on us; for of those who forgive art thou the best:

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 156
records.text: And write down for us what is good in this world, as well as in the world to come, for to thee are we guided." He said, "My chastisement shall fall on whom I will, and my mercy embraceth all things, and I write it down for those who shall fear me, and pay the alms, and believe in our signs,

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 157
records.text: Who shall follow the Apostle, the unlettered32 Prophet-whom they shall find described with them in the Law and Evangel. What is right will he enjoin them, and forbid them what is wrong, and will allow them healthful viands and prohibit the impure, and will ease them of their burden, and of the yokes which were upon them; and those who shall believe in him, and strengthen him, and help him,33 and follow the light34 which hath been sent down with him,- these are they with whom it shall be well."

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 158
records.text: SAY to them: O men! Verily I am God's apostle to you all;

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 159
records.text: Whose is the kingdom of the Heavens and of the Earth! Therefore believe on God but He! He maketh alive and killeth! Therefore believe on God, and his Apostle-the unlettered Prophet-who believeth in God and his word. And follow him that ye may be guided aright.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 160
records.text: And among the people of Moses there is a certain number35 who guide others with truth, and practise what is right according to it.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 161
records.text: And we divided the Israelites into twelve tribes, as nations; and we revealed unto Moses when the people asked drink of him-"Strike the rock with thy staff:" and there gushed forth from it twelve fountains-the men all knew their drinking places. And we caused clouds to overshadow them, and sent down upon them the manna and the quails. . . . "Eat of the good things with which we have supplied you." But it was not us whom they injured, but they injured their own selves:

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 162
records.text: And when it was said to them, "Dwell in this city, and eat therefrom what ye will, and say 'Hittat' (forgiveness), and enter the gate with prostrations; then will we pardon your offences,-we will give increase to the doers of good:"

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 163
records.text: But the ungodly ones among them changed that word into another than that which had been told them:36 therefore sent we forth wrath out of Heaven upon them for their wrong doings.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 164
records.text: And37 ask them about the city that stood by the sea, when its inhabitants broke the Sabbath; when their fish came to them on their Sabbath day appearing openly, but came not to them on the day when they kept no Sabbath. Thus did we make trial of them, for that they were evildoers.38

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 165
records.text: And when some of them said, why warn ye those whom God would destroy or chastise with terrible chastisement? they said, For our own excuse with your Lord; and that they may fear Him.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 166
records.text: And when they forgot their warnings, we delivered those who had forbidden evil; and we inflicted a severe chastisement on those who had done wrong, for that they were evil doers.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 167
records.text: But when they proudly persisted in that which was forbidden, we said to them, "Become scouted apes;" and then thy Lord declared that until the day of the resurrection, he would surely send against them39 (the Jews) those who should evil entreat and chastise them: for prompt is thy Lord to punish; and He is Forgiving, Merciful.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 168
records.text: And we have divided them upon the Earth as peoples: some of them are upright and some are otherwise; and by good things and by evil things have we proved them, to the intent that they might return to us.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 169
records.text: And they have had successors to succeed them: they have inherited the Book: they have received the passing good things of this lower world,40 and say, "It will be forgiven us." Yet if the like good things came to them again, they would again receive them. But hath there not been received on their part a covenant through the Scripture that they should speak nought of God but the truth? And yet they study its contents. But the mansion of the next world hath more value for those who fear God-Do ye not then comprehend?-

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 170
records.text: And who hold fast the Book, and observe prayer: verily, we will not suffer the reward of the righteous to perish.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 171
records.text: And when we shook the mount41 over them as if it had been a shadow, and they thought it falling upon them, . . . "Receive, said we, with steadfastness what we have brought you, and remember what is therein to the end that ye may fear God."

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 172
records.text: And when thy Lord brought forth their descendants from the reins of the sons of Adam and took them to witness against themselves, "Am I not," said He, "your Lord?" They said, "Yes, we witness it." This we did, lest ye should say on the day of Resurrection, "Truly, of this were we heedless, because uninformed;"

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 173
records.text: Or lest ye should say, "Our fathers, indeed, aforetime joined other gods with our God, and we are their seed after them: wilt thou destroy us for the doings of vain men?"

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 174
records.text: Thus make we our signs clear: that haply they may return to God.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 175
records.text: Recite to them42 the history of him43 to whom we vouchsafed our signs, and who departed from them, so that Satan followed him, and he became one of the seduced.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 176
records.text: Had we pleased, we had certainly thereby exalted him; but he crouched to the earth and followed his own lust: his likeness, therefore, is as that of the dog which lolls out his tongue, whether thou chase him away, or leave him alone! Such is the likeness of those who treat our signs as lies. Tell them this tale then, that they may consider.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 177
records.text: Evil the likeness of those who treat our signs as lies! and it is themselves they injure.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 178
records.text: He whom God guideth is the guided, and they whom he misleadeth shall be the lost.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 179
records.text: Many, moreover, of the Djinn and men have we created for Hell. Hearts have they with which they understand not, and eyes have they with which they see not, and ears have they with which they hearken not. They are like the brutes: Yea, they go more astray: these are the heedless.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 180
records.text: Most excellent titles hath God:44 by these call ye on Him, and stand aloof from those who pervert45 his titles. For what they have done shall they be repaid!

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 181
records.text: And among those whom we have created are a people who guide others with truth, and in accordance therewith act justly.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 182
records.text: But as for those who treat our signs as lies, we will gradually bring them down by means of which they know not:

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 183
records.text: And though I lengthen their days, verily, my stratagem shall prove effectual.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 184
records.text: Will they not bethink them that their companion Muhammad is not djinn- possessed? Yes, his office is only that of plain warner.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 185
records.text: Will they not look forth on the realms of the Heaven and of the Earth, and on all things which God hath made, to see whether haply their end be not drawing on? And in what other book will they believe46 who reject the Koran?

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 186
records.text: No other guide for him whom God shall mislead! He will leave them distraught in their wanderings.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 187
records.text: They will ask thee of the Hour-for what time is its coming fixed? SAY: The knowledge of it is only with my Lord: none shall manifest it in its time but He: it is the burden47 of the Heavens and of the Earth: not otherwise than on a sudden will it come on you.48

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 188
records.text: They will ask thee as if thou wast privy to it: SAY: The knowledge of it is with none but God. But most men know not this.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 189
records.text: SAY: I have no control over what may be helpful or hurtful to me, but as God willeth. Had I the knowledge of his secrets, I should revel in the good, and evil should not touch me. But I am only a warner, and an announcer of good tidings to those who believe.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 190
records.text: He it is who hath created you from a single person, and from him brought forth his wife that he might dwell with her: and when he had known her, she bore a light burden, and went about with it; and when it became heavy, they both cried to God their Lord, "If thou give us a perfect child we will surely be of the thankful."

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 191
records.text: Yet when God had given them a perfect child,49 they50 joined partners with Him in return for what he had given them. But high is God above the partners they joined with Him!

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 192
records.text: What! Will they join those with Him who cannot create anything, and are themselves created, and have no power to help them, or to help themselves?

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 193
records.text: And if ye summon them to "the guidance," they will not follow you! It is the same to them whether ye summon them or whether ye hold your peace!

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 194
records.text: Truly they whom ye call on beside God, are, like yourselves, His servants! Call on them then, and let them answer you, if what ye say of them be true!

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 195
records.text: Have they feet to walk with? Have they hands to hold with? Have they eyes to see with? Have they ears to hear with? SAY: Call on these joint gods of yours; then make your plot against me, and delay it not.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 196
records.text: Verily, my Lord is God, who hath sent down "the Book;" and He is the protector of the righteous.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 197
records.text: But they whom ye call on beside Him, can lend you no help, nor can they help themselves:

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 198
records.text: And if ye summon them to "the guidance," they hear you not: thou seest them look towards thee, but they do not see!

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 199
records.text: Make the best of things;51 and enjoin what is just, and withdraw from the ignorant:

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 200
records.text: And if stirrings to evil from Satan stir thee, fly thou for refuge to God: He verily heareth, knoweth!

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 201
records.text: Verily, they who fear God, when some phantom from Satan toucheth them, remember Him, and lo! they see clearly.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 202
records.text: Their Brethren52 will only continue them in error, and cannot preserve themselves from it.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 203
records.text: And when thou bringest not a verse (sign) of the Koran to them, they say, "Hast thou not yet patched it up?53 SAY: I only follow my Lord's utterances to me. This is a clear proof on the part of your Lord, and a guidance and a mercy for those who believe.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 204
records.text: And when the Koran is read, then listen ye to it and keep silence, that haply ye may obtain mercy.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 205
records.text: And think within thine own self on God, with lowliness and with fear and without loud spoken words, at even and at morn; and be not one of the heedless.

records.label: Surah 7 · edition paragraph 206
records.text: Verily they who are round about thy Lord disdain not His service. They praise Him and prostrate themselves before Him.

records.label: Surah 8 · edition paragraph 1
records.text: In the Name of God, the Compassionate, the Merciful

records.label: Surah 8 · edition paragraph 2
records.text: THEY will question thee about THE SPOILS. SAY: The spoils are God's and the apostle's. Therefore, fear God, and settle this among yourselves; and obey God and his apostle, if you are believers.

records.label: Surah 8 · edition paragraph 3
records.text: Believers are they only whose hearts thrill with fear when God is named, and whose faith increaseth at each recital of his signs, and who put their trust in their Lord;

records.label: Surah 8 · edition paragraph 4
records.text: Who observe the prayers, and give alms out of that with which we have supplied them;

records.label: Surah 8 · edition paragraph 5
records.text: These are the believers: their due grade awaiteth them in the presence of their Lord, and forgiveness, and a generous provision.

records.label: Surah 8 · edition paragraph 6
records.text: Remember how thy Lord caused thee to go forth from thy home2 on a mission of truth, and part of the believers were quite averse to it:

records.label: Surah 8 · edition paragraph 7
records.text: They disputed with thee about the truth3 which had been made so clear, as if they were being led forth to death, and saw it before them:

records.label: Surah 8 · edition paragraph 8
records.text: And remember when God promised you that one of the two troops4 should fall to you, and ye desired that they who had no arms should fall to you: but God purposed to prove true the truth of his words, and to cut off the uttermost part ofthe infidels;

records.label: Surah 8 · edition paragraph 9
records.text: That he might prove his truth to be the truth, and bring to nought that which is nought,5 though the impious were averse to it:

records.label: Surah 8 · edition paragraph 10
records.text: When ye sought succour of your Lord, and he answered you, "I will verily aid you with a thousand6 angels, rank on rank:"

records.label: Surah 8 · edition paragraph 11
records.text: And God made this promise as pure good tidings, and to assure your hearts by it: for succour cometh from God alone! Verily God is Mighty, Wise.

records.label: Surah 8 · edition paragraph 12
records.text: Recollect when sleep, a sign of security from Him, fell upon you, and he sent down upon you water from Heaven that he might thereby cleanse you, and cause the pollution of Satan to pass from you, and that he might gird up your hearts, and stablish your feet by it:

records.label: Surah 8 · edition paragraph 13
records.text: When thy Lord spake unto the angels, "I will be with you: therefore stablish ye the faithful. I will cast a dread into the hearts of the infidels." Strike off their heads then, and strike off from them every finger-tip.

records.label: Surah 8 · edition paragraph 14
records.text: This, because they have opposed God and his apostle: And whoso shall oppose God and his apostle. . . . Verily, God will be severe in punishment.

records.label: Surah 8 · edition paragraph 15
records.text: "This for you! Taste it then! and for the infidels is the torture of the fire!"

records.label: Surah 8 · edition paragraph 16
records.text: O ye who believe! when ye meet the marshalled hosts of the infidels, turn not your backs to them:

records.label: Surah 8 · edition paragraph 17
records.text: Whoso shall turn his back to them on that day, unless he turn aside to fight, or to rally to some other troop, shall incur wrath from God: Hell shall be his abode and wretched the journey thither!

records.label: Surah 8 · edition paragraph 18
records.text: So it was not ye who slew them, but God slew them; and those shafts were God's, not thine!7 He would make trial of the faithful by a gracious trial from Himself: Verily, God Heareth, Knoweth.

records.label: Surah 8 · edition paragraph 19
records.text: This befel, that God might also bring to nought the craft of the infidels.

records.label: Surah 8 · edition paragraph 20
records.text: O Meccans! if ye desired a decision, now hath the decision come to you.8 It will be better for you if ye give over the struggle. If ye return to it, we will return; and your forces, though they be many, shall never avail you aught, for God is with the faithful.

records.label: Surah 8 · edition paragraph 21
records.text: O ye faithful! obey God and his apostle, and turn not away from Him, now that ye hear the truth;

records.label: Surah 8 · edition paragraph 22
records.text: And be not like those who say "We hear," when they hear not;

records.label: Surah 8 · edition paragraph 23
records.text: For the vilest beasts in God's sight, are the deaf, the dumb, who understand not.

records.label: Surah 8 · edition paragraph 24
records.text: Had God known any good in them, he would certainly have made them hear. But even if He had made them hear, they would certainly have turned back and withdrawn afar.

records.label: Surah 8 · edition paragraph 25
records.text: O ye faithful! make answer to the appeal of God and his apostle when he calleth you to that which giveth you life. Know that God cometh in between a man and his own heart, and that to him shall ye be gathered.

records.label: Surah 8 · edition paragraph 26
records.text: And be afraid of temptation: the evil doers among you will not be the only ones on whom it will light: And know ye that God is severe in punishment.

records.label: Surah 8 · edition paragraph 27
records.text: And remember when ye were few, and reputed weak in the land:9 ye feared lest men should pluck you away; then was it that He took you in and strengthened you with his help, and supplied you with good things, that haply ye might give thanks.

records.label: Surah 8 · edition paragraph 28
records.text: O ye who believe! deal not falsely with God and his apostle; and be not false in your engagements, with your own knowledge:

records.label: Surah 8 · edition paragraph 29
records.text: And know that your wealth and your children are a temptation; and that God! with Him is a glorious recompense.

records.label: Surah 8 · edition paragraph 30
records.text: O ye who believe! if ye fear God he will make good your deliverance, and will put away your sins from you, and will forgive you. God is of great bounteousness!

records.label: Surah 8 · edition paragraph 31
records.text: And call to mind when the unbelievers plotted against thee, to detain thee prisoner, or to kill thee, or to banish thee: They plotted-but God plotted: and of plotters is God the best!

records.label: Surah 8 · edition paragraph 32
records.text: And oft as our signs were rehearsed to them, they said, "Now have we heard: if we pleased we could certainly utter its like! Yes, it is mere tales of the ancients."

records.label: Surah 8 · edition paragraph 33
records.text: And when they said, "God! if this be the very truth from before thee, rain down stones upon us from Heaven, or lay on us some grievous chastisement."

records.label: Surah 8 · edition paragraph 34
records.text: But God chose not to chastise them while thou wast with them, nor would God chastise them when they sued for pardon.

records.label: Surah 8 · edition paragraph 35
records.text: But because they debarred the faithful from the holy temple, albeit they are not its guardians, nothing is there on their part why God should not chastise them. The Godfearing only are its guardians; but most of them know it not.

records.label: Surah 8 · edition paragraph 36
records.text: And their prayer at the house of God is no other than whistling through the fingers and clapping of the hands-"Taste then the torment, for that ye have been unbelievers."

records.label: Surah 8 · edition paragraph 37
records.text: The infidels spend their riches10 with intent to turn men aside from the way of God: spend it they shall; then shall sighing be upon them, and then shall they be overcome.

records.label: Surah 8 · edition paragraph 38
records.text: And the infidels shall be gathered together into Hell,

records.label: Surah 8 · edition paragraph 39
records.text: That God may separate the bad from the good, and put the bad one upon the other, and heap them all up and put them into Hell! These are they who shall be lost.

records.label: Surah 8 · edition paragraph 40
records.text: SAY to the infidels: If they desist from their unbelief, what is now past shall be forgiven them; but if they return to it, they have already before them11 the doom of the ancients!

records.label: Surah 8 · edition paragraph 41
records.text: Fight then against them till strife be at an end, and the religion be all of it God's. If they desist, verily God beholdeth what they do:

records.label: Surah 8 · edition paragraph 42
records.text: But if they turn their back, know ye that God is your protector: Excellent protector! excellent helper!

records.label: Surah 8 · edition paragraph 43
records.text: And know ye, that when ye have taken any booty, a fifth12 part belongeth to God and to the Apostle, and to the near of kin, and to orphans, and to the poor, and to the wayfarer, if ye believe in God, and in that which we have sent down to our servant on the day of the victory,13 the day of the meeting of the Hosts. Over all things is God potent.

records.label: Surah 8 · edition paragraph 44
records.text: When ye were encamped on the near side of the valley, and they were on the further side, and the caravan was below you, if ye had made an engagement to attack ye would have failed the engagement; but ye were led into action notwithstanding, that God might accomplish the thing destined to be done:

records.label: Surah 8 · edition paragraph 45
records.text: That he who should perish might perish with a clear token14 before him, and that he who liveth might live with it. And verily, God Heareth, Knoweth.

records.label: Surah 8 · edition paragraph 46
records.text: Remember when God shewed them to thee in thy dream, as few: Had he shown them numerous, ye would certainly have become fainthearted, and would certainly have disputed about the matter-But from this God kept you-He knoweth the very secrets of the breast-

records.label: Surah 8 · edition paragraph 47
