records.text: O my people! I ask of you no recompense for this: my recompense is with Him only who hath made me. Will ye not then understand?

records.label: Surah 11 · edition paragraph 55
records.text: O my people! ask pardon of your Lord; then be turned unto Him: He will send down the heavens upon you with copious rains:

records.label: Surah 11 · edition paragraph 56
records.text: And with strength on strength will He increase you: only turn not back with deeds of evil."

records.label: Surah 11 · edition paragraph 57
records.text: They said, "O Houd, thou hast not brought us proofs of thy mission: we will not abandon our gods at thy word, and we believe thee not.

records.label: Surah 11 · edition paragraph 58
records.text: We can only say that some of our gods have smitten thee with evil." Said he, "Now take I God to witness, and do ye also witness, that I am clear of your joining other gods

records.label: Surah 11 · edition paragraph 59
records.text: To God. Conspire then against me all of you, and delay me not.

records.label: Surah 11 · edition paragraph 60
records.text: For I trust in God, my Lord and yours. No single beast is there which he holdeth not by its forelock. Right, truly, is the way in which my Lord goeth.

records.label: Surah 11 · edition paragraph 61
records.text: But if ye turn back, I have already declared to you my message. And my Lord will put another people in your place, nor shall ye at all hurt Him; verily, my Lord keepeth watch over all things."

records.label: Surah 11 · edition paragraph 62
records.text: And when our doom came to be inflicted, we rescued Houd and those who had like faith with Him, by our special mercy: we rescued them from the rigorous chastisement.

records.label: Surah 11 · edition paragraph 63
records.text: These men of Ad gainsaid the signs of their Lord, and rebelled against his messengers, and followed the bidding of every proud contumacious person.

records.label: Surah 11 · edition paragraph 64
records.text: Followed therefore were they in this world by a curse; and in the day of the Resurrection it shall be said to them, "What! Did not Ad disbelieve their Lord?" Was not Ad, the people of Houd, cast far away?

records.label: Surah 11 · edition paragraph 65
records.text: And unto Themoud we sent their Brother Saleh:10-"O my people! said he, worship God: you have no other god than Him. He hath raised you up out of the earth, and hath given you to dwell therein. Ask pardon of him then, and be turned unto him; for thy Lord is nigh, ready to answer."

records.label: Surah 11 · edition paragraph 66
records.text: They said, "O Saleh! our hopes were fixed on thee till now:11 forbiddest thou us to worship what our fathers worshipped? Truly we misdoubt the faith to which thou callest us, as suspicious."

records.label: Surah 11 · edition paragraph 67
records.text: He said, "O my people! what think ye? If I have a revelation from my Lord to support me, and if He hath shewed his mercy on me, who could protect me from God if I rebel against him? Ye would only confer on me increase of ruin.

records.label: Surah 11 · edition paragraph 68
records.text: O my people! this is the she-Camel of God, and a sign unto you. Let her go at large and feed in God's earth, and do her no harm, lest a speedy punishment overtake you."

records.label: Surah 11 · edition paragraph 69
records.text: Yet they hamstrung her: then said he, "Yet three days more enjoy yourselves in your dwellings: this menace will not prove untrue."

records.label: Surah 11 · edition paragraph 70
records.text: And when our sentence came to pass, we rescued Saleh and those who had a like faith with him, by our mercy, from ignominy on that day. Verily, thy Lord is the Strong, the Mighty!

records.label: Surah 11 · edition paragraph 71
records.text: And a violent tempest overtook the wicked, and they were found in the morning prostrate in their dwellings,

records.label: Surah 11 · edition paragraph 72
records.text: As though they had never abode in them. What! Did not Themoud disbelieve his Lord? Was not Themoud utterly cast off?

records.label: Surah 11 · edition paragraph 73
records.text: And our messengers came formerly to Abraham with glad tidings. "Peace," said they. He said, "Peace," and he tarried not, but brought a roasted calf.

records.label: Surah 11 · edition paragraph 74
records.text: And when he saw that their hands touched it not,12 he misliked them, and grew fearful of them. They said, "Fear not, for we are sent to the people of Lot."

records.label: Surah 11 · edition paragraph 75
records.text: His wife was standing by and laughed;13 and we announced Isaac to her; and after Isacc, Jacob.

records.label: Surah 11 · edition paragraph 76
records.text: She said, "Ah, woe is me! shall I bear a son when I am old, and when this my husband is an old man? This truly would be a marvellous thing."

records.label: Surah 11 · edition paragraph 77
records.text: They said, "Marvellest thou at the command of God? God's mercy and blessing be upon you, O people of this house; praise and glory are His due!"

records.label: Surah 11 · edition paragraph 78
records.text: And when Abraham's fear had passed away, and these glad tidings had reached him, he pleaded with us for the people of Lot. Verily, Abraham was right kind, pitiful, relenting.

records.label: Surah 11 · edition paragraph 79
records.text: "O Abraham! desist from this; for already hath the command of thy God gone forth; as for them, a punishment not to be averted is coming on them."

records.label: Surah 11 · edition paragraph 80
records.text: And when our messengers came to Lot, he was grieved for them; and he was too weak to protect them,14 and he said, "This is a day of difficulty."

records.label: Surah 11 · edition paragraph 81
records.text: And his people came rushing on towards him, for aforetime had they wrought this wickedness. He said, "O my people! these my daughters will be purer for you: fear God, and put me not to shame in my guests. Is there no rightminded man among you?"

records.label: Surah 11 · edition paragraph 82
records.text: They said, "Thou knowest now that we need not thy daughters; and thou well knowest what we require."

records.label: Surah 11 · edition paragraph 83
records.text: He said, "Would that I had strength to resist you, or that I could find refuge with some powerful chieftain."15

records.label: Surah 11 · edition paragraph 84
records.text: The Angels said, "O Lot! verily, we are the messengers of thy Lord: they shall not touch thee: depart with thy family in the dead of night, and let not one of you turn back: as for thy wife, on her shall light what shall light on them. Verily, that with which they are threatened is for the morning. Is not the morning near?"

records.label: Surah 11 · edition paragraph 85
records.text: And when our decree came to be executed we turned those cities upside down, and we rained down upon them blocks of claystone one after another, marked16 by thy Lord himself. Nor are they far distant from the wicked Meccans.

records.label: Surah 11 · edition paragraph 86
records.text: And we sent to Madian17 their brother Shoaib. He said, "O my people! worship God: no other God have you than He: give not short weight and measure: I see indeed that ye revel in good things; but I fear for you the punishment of the all-encompassing day.

records.label: Surah 11 · edition paragraph 87
records.text: O my people! give weight and measure with fairness; purloin not other men's goods; and perpetrate not injustice on the earth with corrupt practices:

records.label: Surah 11 · edition paragraph 88
records.text: A residue,18 the gift of God, will be best for you if ye are believers:

records.label: Surah 11 · edition paragraph 89
records.text: But I am not a guardian over you."

records.label: Surah 11 · edition paragraph 90
records.text: They said to him, "O Shoaib! is it thy prayers which enjoin that we should leave what our fathers worshipped, or that we should not do with our substance as pleaseth us? Thou forsooth art the mild, the right director!"

records.label: Surah 11 · edition paragraph 91
records.text: He said, "O my people! How think ye? If I have a clear revelation from my Lord, and if from Himself He hath supplied me with goodly supplies, and if I will not follow you in that which I myself forbid you, do I seek aught but your amendment so far as in me lieth? My sole help is in God. In Him do I trust, and to Him do I turn me.

records.label: Surah 11 · edition paragraph 92
records.text: O my people! let not your opposition to me draw down upon you the like of that which befel the people of Noah, or the people of Houd, or the people of Saleh: and the abodes of the people of Lot are not far distant from you!

records.label: Surah 11 · edition paragraph 93
records.text: Seek pardon of your Lord and be turned unto Him: verily, my Lord is Merciful, Loving.

records.label: Surah 11 · edition paragraph 94
records.text: They said, "O Shoaib! we understand not much of what thou sayest, and we clearly see that thou art powerless among us: were it not for thy family we would have surely stoned thee, nor couldest thou have prevailed against us."

records.label: Surah 11 · edition paragraph 95
records.text: He said, "O my people! think ye more highly of my family than of God? Cast ye Him behind your back, with neglect? Verily, my Lord is round about your actions.

records.label: Surah 11 · edition paragraph 96
records.text: And, O my people! act with what power ye can for my hurt: I verily will act: and ye shall know

records.label: Surah 11 · edition paragraph 97
records.text: On whom shall light a punishment that shall disgrace him, and who is the liar. Await ye; verily I will await with you."

records.label: Surah 11 · edition paragraph 98
records.text: And when our decree came to pass, we delivered Shoaib and his companions in faith, by our mercy: And a violent tempest overtook the wicked, and in the morning they were found prostrate in their houses

records.label: Surah 11 · edition paragraph 99
records.text: As if they had never dwelt in them. Was not Madian swept off even as Themoud had been swept off?

records.label: Surah 11 · edition paragraph 100
records.text: Of old sent we Moses with our signs and with incontestable power to Pharaoh, and to his nobles-who followed the behests of Pharaoh, and, unrighteous were Pharaoh's behests.

records.label: Surah 11 · edition paragraph 101
records.text: He shall head his people on the day of the Resurrection and cause them to descend into the fire: and wretched the descent by which they shall descend!

records.label: Surah 11 · edition paragraph 102
records.text: They were followed by a curse in this world; and in the day of the Resurrection, wretched the gift that shall be given them!

records.label: Surah 11 · edition paragraph 103
records.text: Such, the histories of the cities which we relate to thee. Some of them are standing, others mown down:

records.label: Surah 11 · edition paragraph 104
records.text: We dealt not unfairly by them, but they dealt not fairly by themselves: and their gods on whom they called beside God availed them not at all when thy Lord's behest came to pass. They did but increase their ruin.

records.label: Surah 11 · edition paragraph 105
records.text: Such was thy Lord's grasp19 when he laid that grasp on the cities that had been wicked. Verily his grasp is afflictive, terrible!

records.label: Surah 11 · edition paragraph 106
records.text: Herein truly is a sign for him who feareth the punishment of the latter day. That shall be a day unto which mankind shall be gathered together; that shall be a day witnessed by all creatures.

records.label: Surah 11 · edition paragraph 107
records.text: Nor do we delay it, but until a time appointed.

records.label: Surah 11 · edition paragraph 108
records.text: When that day shall come no one shall speak a word but by His leave, and some shall be miserable and others blessed.

records.label: Surah 11 · edition paragraph 109
records.text: And as for those who shall be consigned to misery-their place the Fire! therein shall they sigh and bemoan them-

records.label: Surah 11 · edition paragraph 110
records.text: Therein shall they abide while the Heavens and the Earth shall last, unless thy Lord shall will it otherwise; verily thy Lord doth what He chooseth.

records.label: Surah 11 · edition paragraph 111
records.text: And as for the blessed ones-their place the Garden! therein shall they abide while the Heavens and the Earth endure, with whatever imperishable boon thy Lord may please to add.

records.label: Surah 11 · edition paragraph 112
records.text: Have thou no doubts therefore concerning that which they worship: they worship but what their fathers worshipped before them: we will surely assign them their portion with nothing lacking.

records.label: Surah 11 · edition paragraph 113
records.text: Of old gave we Moses the Book, and they fell to variance about it. If a decree of respite had not gone forth from thy Lord, there had surely been a decision between them. Thy people also are in suspicious doubts about the Koran.

records.label: Surah 11 · edition paragraph 114
records.text: And truly thy Lord will repay every one according to their works! for He is well aware of what they do.

records.label: Surah 11 · edition paragraph 115
records.text: Go straight on then as thou hast been commanded, and he also who hath turned to God with thee, and let him transgress no more. He beholdeth what ye do.

records.label: Surah 11 · edition paragraph 116
records.text: Lean not on the evil doers lest the Fire lay hold on you. Ye have no protector, save God, and ye shall not be helped against Him.

records.label: Surah 11 · edition paragraph 117
records.text: And observe prayer at early morning, at the close of the day, and at the approach of night; for the good deeds drive away the evil deeds. This is a warning for those who reflect:

records.label: Surah 11 · edition paragraph 118
records.text: And persevere steadfastly, for verily God will not suffer the reward of the righteous to perish.

records.label: Surah 11 · edition paragraph 119
records.text: Were the generations before you, endued with virtue, and who forbad corrupt doings on the earth, more than a few of those whom we delivered? but the evil doers followed their selfish pleasures, and became transgressors.

records.label: Surah 11 · edition paragraph 120
records.text: And thy Lord was not one who would destroy those cities unjustly, when its inhabitants were righteous.

records.label: Surah 11 · edition paragraph 121
records.text: Had thy Lord pleased he would have made mankind of one religion: but those only to whom thy Lord hath granted his mercy will cease to differ. And unto this hath He created them; for the word of thy Lord shall be fulfilled, "I will wholly fill hell with Djinn and men."

records.label: Surah 11 · edition paragraph 122
records.text: And all that we have related to thee of the histories of these Apostles, is to confirm thy heart thereby. By these hath the truth reached thee, and a monition and warning to those who believe.

records.label: Surah 11 · edition paragraph 123
records.text: But say to those who believe not, "Act as ye may and can: we will act our part: and wait ye; we verily will wait."

records.label: Surah 11 · edition paragraph 124
records.text: To God belong the secret things of the Heavens and of the Earth: all things return to him: worship him then and put thy trust in Him: thy Lord is not regardless of your doings.20

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 1
records.text: In the Name of God, the Compassionate, the Merciful

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 2
records.text: ELIF. LAM. RA.1 These are signs of the clear Book.

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 3
records.text: An Arabic Koran have we sent it down, that ye might understand it.

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 4
records.text: In revealing to thee this Koran,2 one of the most beautiful of narratives will we narrate to thee, of which thou hast hitherto been regardless.

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 5
records.text: When Joseph said to his Father, "O my Father! verily I beheld eleven stars and the sun and the moon-beheld them make obeisance to me!"3

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 6
records.text: He said, "O my son! tell not thy vision to thy brethren, lest they plot a plot against thee: for Satan is the manifest foe of man.

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 7
records.text: It is thus that thy Lord shall choose thee and will teach thee the interpretation of dark saying, and will perfect his favours on thee and on the family of Jacob, as of old he perfected it on thy fathers Abraham and Isaac; verily thy Lord is Knowing, Wise!"

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 8
records.text: Now in JOSEPH and his brethren are signs for the enquirers;4

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 9
records.text: When they said, "Surely better loved by our Father, than we, who are more in number, is Joseph and his brother; verily, our father hath clearly erred.

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 10
records.text: Slay ye Joseph! or drive him to some other land, and on you alone shall your father's face be set! and after this, ye shall live as upright persons."

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 11
records.text: One of them said, "Slay not Joseph, but cast him down to the bottom of the well: if ye do so, some wayfarers will take him up."

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 12
records.text: They said, "O our Father! why dost thou not entrust us with Joseph? indeed we mean him well.

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 13
records.text: Send him with us to-morrow that he may enjoy himself and sport: we will surely keep him safely."

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 14
records.text: He said, "Verily, your taking him away will grieve me; and I fear lest while ye are heedless of him the wolf devour him."

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 15
records.text: They said, "Surely if the wolf devour him, and we so many, we must in that case be weak indeed."5

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 16
records.text: And when they went away with him they agreed to place him at the bottom of the well. And We revealed to him, "Thou wilt yet tell them of this their deed, when they shall not know thee."

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 17
records.text: And they came at nightfall to their father weeping.

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 18
records.text: They said, "O our Father! of a truth, we went to run races, and we left Joseph with our clothes, and the wolf devoured him: but thou wilt not believe us even though we speak the truth."

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 19
records.text: And they brought his shirt with false blood upon it. He said, "Nay, but yourselves have managed this affair.6 But patience is seemly: and the help of God is to be implored that I may bear what you tell me."

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 20
records.text: And wayfarers came and sent their drawer of water,7 and he let down his bucket. "Good news!"8 said he, "This is a youth!" And they kept his case secret, to make merchandise of him. But God knew what they did.

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 21
records.text: And they sold him for a paltry price-for some dirhems counted down, and at no high rate did they value him.

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 22
records.text: And he who bought him-an Egyptian-said to his wife, "Treat him hospitably; haply he may be useful to us, or we may adopt him as a son." Thus did we settle Joseph in the land, and we instructed him in the interpretation of dark sayings, for God is equal to his purpose; but most men know it not.

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 23
records.text: And when he had reached his age of strength we bestowed on him judgment and knowledge; for thus do we recompense the well doers.

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 24
records.text: And she in whose house he was conceived a passion for him, and she shut the doors and said, "Come hither." He said, "God keep me! Verily, my lord hath given me a good home: and the injurious shall not prosper."

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 25
records.text: But she longed for him; and he had longed for her had he not seen a token from his lord.9 Thus we averted evil and defilement from him, for he was one of our sincere servants.

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 26
records.text: And they both made for the door, and she rent his shirt behind; and at the door they met her lord. "What," said she, "shall be the recompense of him who would do evil to thy family, but a prison10 or a sore punishment?"

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 27
records.text: He said, "She solicited me to evil." And a witness out of her own family11 witnessed: "If his shirt be rent in front she speaketh truth, and he is a liar:

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 28
records.text: But if his shirt be rent behind, she lieth and he is true."

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 29
records.text: And when his lord saw his shirt torn behind, he said, "This is one of your devices! verily your devices are great!

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 30
records.text: Joseph! leave this affair. And thou, O wife, ask pardon for thy crime, for thou hast sinned."

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 31
records.text: And in the city, the women said, "The wife of the Prince hath solicited her servant: he hath fired her with his love: but we clearly see her manifest error."

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 32
records.text: And when she heard of their cabal, she sent to them and got ready a banquet for them, and gave each one of them a knife, and said, "Joseph shew thyself to them." And when they saw him they were amazed at him, and cut their hands,12 and said, "God keep us! This is no man! This is no other than a noble angel!"

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 33
records.text: She said, "This is he about whom ye blamed me. I wished him to yield to my desires, but he stood firm. But if he obey not my command, he shall surely be cast into prison, and become one of the despised."

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 34
records.text: He said, "O my Lord! I prefer the prison to compliance with their bidding: but unless thou turn away their snares from me, I shall play the youth with them, and become one of the unwise."

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 35
records.text: And his Lord heard him and turned aside their snares from him: for he is the Hearer, the Knower.

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 36
records.text: Yet resolved they, even after they had seen the signs of his innocence, to imprison him for a time.

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 37
records.text: And there came into the prison with him two youths. Said one of them, "Methought in my dream that I was pressing grapes." And the other said, "I dreamed that I was carrying bread on my head, of which the birds did eat. Declare to us the interpretation of this, for we see thou art a virtuous person."

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 38
records.text: He said, "There shall not come to you in a dream any food wherewith ye shall be fed, but I will acquaint you with its interpretation ere it come to pass to you. This is a part of that which my Lord hath taught me: for I have abandoned the religion13 of those who believe not in God and who deny the life to come;

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 39
records.text: And I follow the religion of my fathers, Abraham and Isaac and Jacob. We may not associate aught with God. This is of God's bounty towards us and towards mankind: but the greater part of mankind are not thankful.

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 40
records.text: O my two fellow prisoners! are sundry lords best, or God, the One, the Mighty?

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 41
records.text: Ye worship beside him mere names which ye have named, ye and your fathers, for which God hath not sent down any warranty. Judgment belongeth to God alone. He hath bidden you worship none but Him. This is the right faith: but most men know it not.

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 42
records.text: O my two fellow prisoners! as to one of you, he will serve wine unto his Lord: but as to the other, he will be crucified and the birds shall eat from off his head. The matter is decreed concerning which ye enquire."

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 43
records.text: And he said unto him who he judged would be set at large, "Remember me with thy lord." But Satan caused him to forget the remembrance of his Lord,14 so he remained some years in prison.

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 44
records.text: And the King said, "Verily, I saw in a dream seven fat kine which seven lean devoured; and seven green ears and other withered. O nobles, teach me my vision, if a vision ye are able to expound."

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 45
records.text: They said, "They are confused dreams, nor know we aught of the unravelling of dreams."

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 46
records.text: And he of the twain who had been set at large, said, "I will tell you the interpretation; let me go for it."

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 47
records.text: "Joseph, man of truth! teach us of the seven fat kine which seven lean devoured, and of the seven green ears, and other withered, that I may return to the men, and that they may be informed."

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 48
records.text: He said, "Ye shall sow seven years as is your wont, and the corn which ye reap leave ye in its ear, except a little of which ye shall eat.

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 49
records.text: Then after that shall come seven grievous years which shall eat what ye have stored for them, except a little which ye shall have kept.

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 50
records.text: Then shall come after this a year, in which men shall have rain, and in which they shall press the grape."

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 51
records.text: And the King said, "Bring him to me."15 And when the messenger came to Joseph he said, "Go back to thy lord, and ask him what meant the women who cut their hands, for my lord well knoweth the snare they laid."

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 52
records.text: Then said the Prince to the women, "What was your purpose when ye solicited Joseph?" They said, "God keep us! we know not any ill of him." The wife of the Prince said, "Now doth the truth appear. It was I who would have led him into unlawful love, and he is one of the truthful."

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 53
records.text: "By this" (said Joseph) "may my lord know that I did not in his absence play him false, and that God guideth not the machinations of deceivers.

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 54
records.text: Yet I hold not myself clear, for the heart is prone to evil, save theirs on whom my Lord hath mercy; for gracious is my Lord, Merciful."

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 55
records.text: And the King said, "Bring him to me: I will take him for my special service." And when he had spoken with him he said, "From this day shalt thou be with us, invested with place and trust."

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 56
records.text: He said, "Set me over the granaries of the land,16 I will be their prudent keeper!"

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 57
records.text: Thus did we stablish Joseph in the land that he might house himself therein at pleasure. We bestow our favours on whom we will, and suffer not the reward of the righteous to perish.

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 58
records.text: And truly the recompense of the life to come is better, for those who have believed and feared God.

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 59
records.text: And Joseph's brethren came and went in to him and he knew them, but they recognised him not.

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 60
records.text: And when he had provided them with their provision, he said, "Bring me your brother from your father. See ye not that I fill the measure, and am the best of hosts?

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 61
records.text: But if ye bring him not to me, then no measure of corn shall there be for you from me, nor shall ye come near me."

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 62
records.text: They said, "We will ask him of his father, and we will surely do it."

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 63
records.text: Said he to his servants, "Put their money into their camel-packs, that they may perceive it when they have returned to their family: haply they will come back to us."

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 64
records.text: And when they returned to their father, they said, "O, our father! corn is withholden from us: send, therefore, our brother with us and we shall have our measure; and all care of him will we take."

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 65
records.text: He said, "Shall I entrust you with him otherwise than as I before entrusted you with his brother? But God is the best guardian, and of those who shew compassion He is the most compassionate."

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 66
records.text: And when they opened their goods they found their money had been returned to them. They said, "O, our father, what more can we desire? Here is our money returned to us; we will provide corn for our families, and will take care of our brother, and shall receive a camel's burden more of corn. This is an easy quantity."17

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 67
records.text: He said, "I will not send him with you but on your oath before God that ye will, indeed, bring him back to me, unless hindrances encompass you." And when they had given him their pledge, he said, "God is witness of what we say."

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 68
records.text: And he said, "O, my sons! Enter not by one gate, but enter by different gates.18 Yet can I not help you against aught decreed by God: judgment belongeth to God alone. In Him put I my trust, and in Him let the trusting trust."

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 69
records.text: And when they entered as their father had bidden them, it did not avert from them anything decreed of God; but it only served to satisfy a desire in the soul of Jacob which he had charged them to perform; for he was possessed of knowledge which we had taught him; but most men have not that knowledge.

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 70
records.text: And when they came in to Joseph, he took his brother to him. He said, "Verily, I am thy brother. Be not thou grieved for what they did."19

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 71
records.text: And when he had provided them with their provisions, he placed his drinking cup in his brother's camel-pack. Then a crier cried after them, "O travellers! ye are surely thieves."

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 72
records.text: They turned back to them and said, "What is that ye miss?"

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 73
records.text: "We miss," said they, "the prince's cup. For him who shall restore it, a camel's load of corn! I pledge myself for it."

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 74
records.text: They said, "By God! ye know certainly that we came not to do wrong20 in the land and we have not been thieves."

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 75
records.text: "What," said the Egyptians, "shall be the recompense of him who hath stolen it, if ye be found liars?"

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 76
records.text: They said, "That he in whose camel-pack it shall be found be given up to you in satisfaction for it. Thus recompense we the unjust."

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 77
records.text: And Joseph began with their sacks, before the sack of his brother, and then from the sack of his brother he drew it out. This stratagem did we suggest to Joseph. By the King's law he had no power to seize his brother, had not God pleased. We uplift into grades of wisdom whom we will. And there is one knowing above every one else endued with knowledge.

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 78
records.text: They said, "If he steal, a brother of his hath stolen heretofore."21 But Joseph kept his secret, and did not discover it to them. Said he, aside, "Ye are in the worse condition. And God well knoweth what ye state."

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 79
records.text: They said, "O Prince! Verily he hath a very aged father; in his stead, therefore, take one of us, for we see that thou art a generous person."

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 80
records.text: He said, "God forbid that we should take but him with whom our property was found, for then should we act unjustly."

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 81
records.text: And when they despaired of Benjamin, they went apart for counsel. The eldest of them said, "Know ye not how that your father hath taken a pledge from you before God, and how formerly ye failed in duty with regard to Joseph? I will not quit the land till my father give me leave, or God decide for me; for of those who decide is He the best.

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 82
records.text: Return ye to your father and say, 'O our father! Verily, thy son hath stolen: we bear witness only of what we know: we could not guard against the unforeseen.

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 83
records.text: Enquire for thyself in the city where we have been, and of the caravan with which we have arrived; and we are surely speakers of the truth.'

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 84
records.text: He said, "Nay, ye have arranged all this among yourselves: But patience is seemly: God, may be, will bring them back to me together; for he is the Knowing, the Wise."

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 85
records.text: And he turned away from them and said, "Oh! how I am grieved for Joseph!" and his eyes became white with grief, for he bore a silent sorrow.

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 86
records.text: They said, "By God thou wilt only cease to think of Joseph when thou art at the point of death, or dead."

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 87
records.text: He said, "I only plead my grief and my sorrow to God: but I know from God what ye know not:22

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 88
records.text: Go, my sons, and seek tidings of Joseph and his brother, and despair not of God's mercy, for none but the unbelieving despair of the mercy of God."

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 89
records.text: And when they came in to Joseph, they said, "O Prince, distress hath reached us and our family, and little is the money that we have brought. But give us full measure, and bestow it as alms, for God will recompense the almsgivers."

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 90
records.text: He said, "Know ye what ye did to Joseph and his brother in your ignorance?"

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 91
records.text: They said, "Canst thou indeed be Joseph?" He said, "I am Joseph, and this is my brother. Now hath God been gracious to us. For whoso feareth God and endureth. . . . God verily will not suffer the reward of the righteous to perish!"

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 92
records.text: They said, "By God! now hath God chosen thee above us, and we have indeed been sinners!"

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 93
records.text: He said, "No blame be on you this day. God will forgive you, for He is the most merciful of those who shew mercy.

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 94
records.text: Go ye with this my shirt and throw it on my father's face, and he shall recover his sight: and bring me all your family."

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 95
records.text: And when the caravan was departed, their father said, "I surely perceive the smell of Joseph:23 think ye that I dote?"

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 96
records.text: They said, "By God, it is thy old mistake."

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 97
records.text: And when the bearer of good tidings came, he cast it on his face, and Jacob's eyesight returned."

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 98
records.text: Then he said, "Did I not tell you that I knew from God what ye knew not?"

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 99
records.text: They said, "Our father, ask pardon for our crimes for us, for we have indeed been sinners."

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 100
records.text: He said, "I will ask your pardon of my Lord, for he is Gracious, Merciful."

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 101
records.text: And when they came into Joseph he took his parents24 to him, and said, "Enter ye Egypt, if God will, secure."

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 102
records.text: And he raised his parents to the seat of state, and they fell down bowing themselves unto him. Then said he, "O my father, this is the meaning of my dream of old. My Lord hath now made it true, and he hath surely been gracious to me, since he took me forth from the prison, and hath brought you up out of the desert, after that Satan had stirred up strife between me and my brethren; for my Lord is gracious to whom He will; for He is the Knowing, the Wise.

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 103
records.text: O my Lord, thou hast given me dominion, and hast taught me to expound dark sayings. Maker of the Heavens and of the Earth! My guardian art thou in this world and in the next! Cause thou me to die a Muslim, and join me with the just."

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 104
records.text: This is one of the secret histories25 which we reveal unto thee. Thou wast not present with Joseph's brethren when they conceived their design and laid their plot: but the greater part of men, though thou long for it, will not believe.

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 105
records.text: Thou shalt not ask of them any recompense for this message. It is simply an instruction for all mankind.

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 106
records.text: And many as are the signs in the Heavens and on the Earth, yet they will pass them by, and turn aside from them:

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 107
records.text: And most of them believe not in God, without also joining other deities with Him.

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 108
records.text: What! Are they sure that the overwhelming chastisement of God shall not come upon them, or that that Hour shall not come upon them suddenly, while they are unaware?

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 109
records.text: SAY: This is my way: resting on a clear proof, I call you to God, I and whoso followeth me: and glory be to God! I am not one of those who add other deities to Him.

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 110
records.text: Never before thee have we sent any but men, chosen out of the people of the cities, to whom we made revelations. Will they not journey through the land, and see what hath been the end of those who were before them? But the mansions of the next life shall be better for those who fear God. Will they not then comprehend?

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 111
records.text: When at last the Apostles lost all hope, and deemed that they were reckoned as liars, our aid reached them, and we delivered whom we would; but our vengeance was not averted from the wicked.

records.label: Surah 12 · edition paragraph 112
records.text: Certainly in their histories is an example for men of understanding. This is no new tale of fiction, but a confirmation of previous scriptures, and an explanation of all things, and guidance and mercy to those who believe.

records.label: Surah 13 · edition paragraph 1
records.text: In the Name of God, the Compassionate, the Merciful

records.label: Surah 13 · edition paragraph 2
records.text: ELIF. LAM. MIM. RA.1 These, the signs of the Book! And that which hath been sent down to thee from thy Lord is the very truth: But the greater part of men will not believe.

records.label: Surah 13 · edition paragraph 3
records.text: It is God who hath reared the Heavens without pillars thou canst behold; then mounted his throne, and imposed laws on the sun and moon: each travelleth to its appointed goal. He ordereth all things. He maketh his signs clear, that ye may have firm faith in a meeting with your Lord.

records.label: Surah 13 · edition paragraph 4
records.text: And He it is who hath outstretched the earth, and placed on it the firm mountains, and rivers: and of every fruit He hath placed on it two kinds: He causeth the night to enshroud the day. Verily in this are signs for those who reflect.

records.label: Surah 13 · edition paragraph 5
records.text: And on the earth hard by each other are its various portions: gardens of grapes and corn, and palm trees single or clustered. Though watered by the same water, yet some make we more excellent as food than other: Verily in all this are signs for those who understand.

records.label: Surah 13 · edition paragraph 6
records.text: If ever thou dost marvel, marvellous surely is their saying, "What! when we have become dust, shall we be restored in a new creation?"

records.label: Surah 13 · edition paragraph 7
records.text: These are they who in their Lord believe not: these! the collars shall be on their necks; and these shall be inmates of the fire, to abide therein for aye.

records.label: Surah 13 · edition paragraph 8
records.text: To hasten evil rather than good will they challenge thee: but, before their time have been like examples. Full, truly, of mercy is thy Lord unto men, despite their sins; but verily, thy Lord is right vehement to punish.

records.label: Surah 13 · edition paragraph 9
records.text: And they who believe not say: "If a sign from his Lord be not sent down to him . . . !" Thou art a warner only. And every people hath its guide.

records.label: Surah 13 · edition paragraph 10
records.text: God knoweth the burden of every female, and how much their wombs lessen and enlarge: with Him everything is by measure:

records.label: Surah 13 · edition paragraph 11
records.text: Knower of the Hidden and the Manifest! the Great! the Most High!

records.label: Surah 13 · edition paragraph 12
records.text: Alike to Him is that person among you who concealeth his words, and he that telleth them abroad: he who hideth him in the night, and he who cometh forth in the day.

records.label: Surah 13 · edition paragraph 13
records.text: Each hath a succession of Angels before him and behind him, who watch over him by God's behest. Verily, God will not change his gifts to men, till they change what is in themselves: and when God willeth evil unto men, there is none can turn it away, nor have they any protector beside Him.

records.label: Surah 13 · edition paragraph 14
records.text: He it is who maketh the lightning to shine unto you; for fear and hope: and who bringeth up the laden clouds.

records.label: Surah 13 · edition paragraph 15
records.text: And the THUNDER uttereth his praise, and the Angels also, for awe of Him: and he sendeth his bolts and smiteth with them whom he will2 while they are wrangling about God! Mighty is he in prowess.

records.label: Surah 13 · edition paragraph 16
records.text: Prayer is His of right: but these deities to whom they pray beside Him give them no answer, otherwise than as he is answered who stretcheth forth his hands to the water that it may reach his mouth, when it cannot reach it! The prayer of the Infidels only wandereth, and is lost.

records.label: Surah 13 · edition paragraph 17
records.text: And unto God doth all in the Heavens and on the Earth bow down in worship, willingly or by constraint: their very shadows also morn and even!

records.label: Surah 13 · edition paragraph 18
records.text: SAY: Who is Lord of the Heavens and of the Earth? SAY: God. SAY: Why then have ye taken beside Him protectors, who even for their own selves have no power for help or harm? SAY: What! shall the blind and the seeing be held equal? Shall the darkness and the light be held equal? Or have they given associates to God who have created as He hath created, so that their creation appear to them like His? SAY: God is the Creator of all things! He is the One! the Conquering!

records.label: Surah 13 · edition paragraph 19
records.text: He sendeth down the rain from Heaven: then flow the torrents in their due measure, and the flood beareth along a swelling foam. And from the metals which are molten in the fire for the sake of ornaments or utensils, a like scum ariseth. In this way doth God depict (set forth) truth and falsehood. As to the foam, it is quickly gone: and as to what is useful to man, it remaineth on the earth. Thus doth God set forth comparisons! To those who respond to their Lord shall be an excellent reward; but those who respond not to his call, had they all that the earth containeth twice over, they would surely give it for their ransom. Evil their reckoning! and Hell their home! And wretched the bed!

records.label: Surah 13 · edition paragraph 20
records.text: Shall he then who knoweth that what hath been sent down to thee from thy Lord is the truth, act like him who is blind? Men of insight only will bear this in mind,

records.label: Surah 13 · edition paragraph 21
records.text: Who fulfil their pledge to God, and break not their compact:

records.label: Surah 13 · edition paragraph 22
records.text: And who join together what God hath bidden to be joined, and who fear their Lord, and dread an ill reckoning;

records.label: Surah 13 · edition paragraph 23
records.text: And who, from desire to see the face of their Lord, are constant amid trials, and observe prayer and give alms, in secret and openly, out of what we have bestowed upon them, and turn aside evil by good: for these is the recompense of that abode,

records.label: Surah 13 · edition paragraph 24
records.text: Gardens of Eden-into which they shall enter together with the just of their fathers, and their wives, and their descendants: and the angels shall go in unto them at every portal:

records.label: Surah 13 · edition paragraph 25
records.text: "Peace be with you!" say they, "because ye have endured all things!" Charming the recompense of their abode!

records.label: Surah 13 · edition paragraph 26
records.text: But those who, after having contracted it, break their covenant with God, and cut asunder what God hath bidden to be united, and commit misdeeds on the earth, these, a curse awaiteth them, and an ill abode!

records.label: Surah 13 · edition paragraph 27
records.text: God is open-handed with supplies to whom he will, or is sparing. They rejoice in the life that now is, but this present life is but a passing good, in respect of the life to come!3

records.label: Surah 13 · edition paragraph 28
records.text: And they who believe not say, "Unless a sign be sent down to him from his Lord. . . ." SAY: God truly will mislead whom he will; and He will guide to Himself him who turneth to Him,

records.label: Surah 13 · edition paragraph 29
records.text: Those who believe, and whose hearts rest securely on the thought of God. What! Shall not men's hearts repose in the thought of God? They who believe and do the things that be right-blessedness awaiteth them, and a goodly home.

records.label: Surah 13 · edition paragraph 30
records.text: Thus have we sent thee to a people whom other peoples have preceded, that thou mightest rehearse to them our revelations to thee. Yet they believe not on the God of Mercy.4 SAY: He is my Lord. There is no God but He. In Him do I put my trust. To Him must I return.

records.label: Surah 13 · edition paragraph 31
records.text: If there were a Koran by which the mountains could be set in motion, or the earth cleft, or the dead be made to speak ! But all sovereignty is in the hands of God. Do then believers doubt5 that had He pleased God would certainly have guided all men aright?

records.label: Surah 13 · edition paragraph 32
records.text: Misfortune shall not cease to light on the unbelievers for what they have done, or to take up its abode hard by their dwellings, until the threat of God come to pass. Verily, God will not fail his plighted word.

records.label: Surah 13 · edition paragraph 33
records.text: Before thee indeed have apostles been mocked at; but though I bore long with the unbelievers, at last I seized upon them;-and how severe was my punishment!

records.label: Surah 13 · edition paragraph 34
records.text: Who is it then that is standing over every soul to mark its actions? Yet have they set up associates with God. SAY: Name them. What! Would ye inform God of that which He knoweth not on the Earth? Or are they not a mere empty name? But prepared of old for the infidels was this fraud of theirs; and they are turned aside from the path; and whom God causeth to err, no guide shall there be for him!

records.label: Surah 13 · edition paragraph 35
records.text: Chastisement awaiteth them in this present life, and more grievous shall be the chastisement of the next: and none shall screen them from God.

records.label: Surah 13 · edition paragraph 36
records.text: A picture of the Paradise which God hath promised to them that fear Him. The rivers flow beneath its bowers: its food and its shades are perpetual. This is the reward of those who fear God; but the reward of the unbelievers is the Fire.

records.label: Surah 13 · edition paragraph 37
records.text: They to whom we have given the Book rejoice6 in what hath been sent down to thee; yet some are banded together who deny a part of it. SAY: I am commanded to worship God, and not to associate any creature with Him. On Him do I call, and to Him shall I return.

records.label: Surah 13 · edition paragraph 38
records.text: Thus, then, as a code in the Arabic tongue have we sent down the Koran; and truly, if after the knowledge that hath reached thee thou follow their desires, thou shalt have no guardian nor protector against God.

records.label: Surah 13 · edition paragraph 39
records.text: Apostles truly have we already sent before thee, and wives and offspring have we given them. Yet no apostle had come with miracles unless by the leave of God. To each age its Book.

records.label: Surah 13 · edition paragraph 40
records.text: What He pleaseth will God abrogate or confirm: for with Him is the source of revelation.7

records.label: Surah 13 · edition paragraph 41
records.text: Moreover, whether we cause thee to see the fulfilment of part of our menaces, or whether we take thee hence, verily, thy work is preaching only, and ours to take account.

records.label: Surah 13 · edition paragraph 42
records.text: See they not that we come into their land and cut short its borders?8 God pronounceth a doom, and there is none to reverse his doom. And swift is He to take account.

records.label: Surah 13 · edition paragraph 43
records.text: Those who lived before them made plots: but all plotting is controlled by God: He knoweth the works of every one, and the infidels shall know whose will be the recompense of the abode.

records.label: Surah 13 · edition paragraph 44
records.text: The infidels, moreover, will say; Thou art not sent of God. SAY: God is witness enough betwixt me and you, and, whoever hath knowledge of the Book.

records.label: Surah 14 · edition paragraph 1
records.text: In the Name of God, the Compassionate, the Merciful

records.label: Surah 14 · edition paragraph 2
records.text: ELIF. LAM. RA. This Book have we sent down to thee that by their Lord's permission thou mayest bring men out of darkness into light, into the path of the Mighty, the Glorious-

records.label: Surah 14 · edition paragraph 3
records.text: Of God; to whom belongeth whatever is in the Heavens and whatever is on the Earth: and woe! for their terrible punishment, to the infidels,

records.label: Surah 14 · edition paragraph 4
records.text: Who love the life that now is, above that which is to come, and mislead from the way of God, and seek to make it crooked. These are in a far-gone error.

records.label: Surah 14 · edition paragraph 5
records.text: And in order that He might speak plainly to them, we have not sent any Apostle, save with the speech of his own people; but God misleadeth whom He will, and whom He will he guideth: and He is the Mighty, the Wise.

records.label: Surah 14 · edition paragraph 6
records.text: Of old did we send Moses with our signs: and said to him, "Bring forth thy people from the darkness into the light, and remind them of the days of God." Verily, in this are signs for every patient, grateful person:

records.label: Surah 14 · edition paragraph 7
records.text: When Moses said to his people, "Remember the kindness of God to you, when he rescued you from the family of Pharaoh who laid on you a cruel affliction, slaughtering your male children, and suffering only your females to live." In this was a sore trial from your Lord-

records.label: Surah 14 · edition paragraph 8
records.text: And when your Lord caused it to be heard that, "If we render thanks then will I surely increase you more and more: but if ye be thankless. . . . Verily, right terrible my chastisement."

records.label: Surah 14 · edition paragraph 9
records.text: And Moses said, "If ye and all who are on the Earth be thankless, yet truly God is passing Rich, and worthy of all praise."

records.label: Surah 14 · edition paragraph 10
records.text: Hath not the story reached you of those who were before you, the people of Noah, and Ad, and Themoud,

records.label: Surah 14 · edition paragraph 11
records.text: And of those who lived after them? None knoweth them but God. When their prophets came to them with proofs of their mission, they put their hands on their mouths and said, "In sooth, we believe not your message; and in sooth, of that to which you bid us, we are in doubt, as of a thing suspicious."

records.label: Surah 14 · edition paragraph 12
records.text: Their prophets said: "Is there any doubt concerning God, maker of the Heavens and of the Earth, who calleth you that He may pardon your sins, and respite you until an appointed time?"

records.label: Surah 14 · edition paragraph 13
records.text: They said, "Ye are but men like us: fain would ye turn us from our fathers' worship. Bring us therefore some clear proof."

records.label: Surah 14 · edition paragraph 14
records.text: Their Apostles said to them, "We are indeed but men like you. But God bestoweth favours on such of his servants as he pleaseth, and it is not in our power to bring you any special proof,

records.label: Surah 14 · edition paragraph 15
records.text: But by the leave of God. In God therefore let the faithful trust.

records.label: Surah 14 · edition paragraph 16
records.text: And why should we not put our trust in God, since He hath already guided us in our ways. We will certainly bear with constancy the harm you would do to us. In God let the trustful trust."

records.label: Surah 14 · edition paragraph 17
records.text: And they who believed not said to their Apostles, "Forth from our land will we surely drive you, or, to our religion shall ye return." Then their Lord revealed to them, "We will certainly destroy the wicked doers,

records.label: Surah 14 · edition paragraph 18
records.text: And we shall certainly cause you to dwell in the land after them. This for him who dreadeth the appearance at my judgment-seat and who dreadeth my menace!"

records.label: Surah 14 · edition paragraph 19
records.text: Then sought they help from God, and every proud rebellious one perished:

records.label: Surah 14 · edition paragraph 20
records.text: Hell is before him: and of tainted water shall he be made to drink:

records.label: Surah 14 · edition paragraph 21
records.text: He shall sup it and scarce swallow it for loathing; and Death shall assail him on every side, but he shall not die: and before him shall be seen a grievous torment.

records.label: Surah 14 · edition paragraph 22
records.text: A likeness of those who believe not in their Lord. Their works are like ashes which the wind scattereth on a stormy day: no advantage shall they gain from their works. This is the far-gone wandering.

records.label: Surah 14 · edition paragraph 23
records.text: Seest thou not that in truth1 hath God created the Heavens and the Earth? Were such his pleasure He could make you pass away, and cause a new creation to arise.

records.label: Surah 14 · edition paragraph 24
records.text: And this would not be hard for God.

records.label: Surah 14 · edition paragraph 25
records.text: All mankind shall come forth before God; and the weak shall say to the men of might, "Verily, we were your followers: will ye not then relieve us of some part of the vengeance of God?"

records.label: Surah 14 · edition paragraph 26
records.text: They shall say, "If God had guided us, we surely had guided you. It is now all one whether we be impatient, or endure with patience. We have no escape."

records.label: Surah 14 · edition paragraph 27
records.text: And after doom hath been given, Satan shall say, "Verily, God promised you a promise of truth: I, too, made you a promise, but I deceived you. Yet I had no power over you:

records.label: Surah 14 · edition paragraph 28
records.text: But I only called you and ye answered me. Blame not me then, but blame yourselves: I cannot aid you, neither can ye aid me. I never believed that I was His equal with whom ye joined me."2 As for the evil doers, a grievous torment doth await them.

records.label: Surah 14 · edition paragraph 29
records.text: But they who shall have believed and done the things that be right, shall be brought into gardens beneath which the rivers flow: therein shall they abide for ever by the permission of their Lord: their greeting therein shall be "Peace."

records.label: Surah 14 · edition paragraph 30
records.text: Seest thou not to what God likeneth a good word?3 To a good tree: its root firmly fixed, and its branches in the Heaven:

records.label: Surah 14 · edition paragraph 31
records.text: Yielding its fruit in all seasons by the will of its Lord. God setteth forth these similitudes to men that haply they may reflect.

records.label: Surah 14 · edition paragraph 32
records.text: And an evil word is like an evil tree torn up from the face of the earth, and without strength to stand.

records.label: Surah 14 · edition paragraph 33
records.text: Those who believe shall God stablish by his steadfast word both in this life and in that which is to come: but the wicked shall He cause to err: God doth his pleasure.

records.label: Surah 14 · edition paragraph 34
records.text: Hast thou not beholden those who repay the goodness of God with infidelity, and sink their people into the abode of perdition-

records.label: Surah 14 · edition paragraph 35
records.text: Hell? Therein shall they be burned; and wretched the dwelling!

records.label: Surah 14 · edition paragraph 36
records.text: They set up compeers with God in order to mislead man from his way. SAY: Enjoy your pleasures yet awhile, but assuredly, your going hence shall be into the fire.

records.label: Surah 14 · edition paragraph 37
records.text: Speak to my servants who have believed, that they observe prayer, and give alms of that with which we have supplied them, both privately and openly, ere the day come when there shall be neither traffic nor friendship.

records.label: Surah 14 · edition paragraph 38
records.text: It is God who hath created the Heavens and the Earth, and sendeth down water from the Heaven, and so bringeth forth the fruits for your food: And He hath subjected to you the ships, so that by His command, they pass through the sea; and He hath subjected the rivers to you: and He hath subjected to you the sun and the moon in their constant courses: and He hath subjected the day and the night to you: of everything which ye ask Him, giveth He to you; and if ye would reckon up the favours of God, ye cannot count them! Surely man is unjust, ungrateful!

records.label: Surah 14 · edition paragraph 39
records.text: ABRAHAM said, "O Lord make this land secure, and turn aside me and my children from serving idols:

records.label: Surah 14 · edition paragraph 40
records.text: For many men, O my Lord, have they led astray. But whosoever shall follow me, he truly shall be of me; and whosoever shall disobey me. . . . Thou truly art Gracious, Merciful.

records.label: Surah 14 · edition paragraph 41
records.text: O our Lord! verily I have settled some of my offspring in an unfruitful valley, nigh to thy holy house;4 O our Lord, that they may strictly observe prayer! Make thou therefore the hearts of men to yearn toward them, and supply them with fruits that they may be thankful.

records.label: Surah 14 · edition paragraph 42
records.text: O our Lord! thou truly knowest what we hide and what we bring to light; nought on earth or in heaven is hidden from God. Praise be to God who hath given me, in my old age, Ismael and Isaac! My Lord is the hearer of prayer.

records.label: Surah 14 · edition paragraph 43
records.text: Lord! grant that I and my posterity may observe prayer. O our Lord! and grant this my petition. O our Lord! forgive me and my parents and the faithful, on the day wherein account shall be taken."

records.label: Surah 14 · edition paragraph 44
records.text: Think thou not that God is regardless of the deeds of the wicked. He only respiteth them to the day on which all eyes shall stare up with terror:

records.label: Surah 14 · edition paragraph 45
records.text: They hasten forward in fear; their heads upraised in supplication; their looks riveted; and their hearts a blank. Warn men therefore of the day when the punishment shall overtake them,

records.label: Surah 14 · edition paragraph 46
records.text: And when the evil doers shall say, "O our Lord! respite us yet a little while:5

records.label: Surah 14 · edition paragraph 47
records.text: To thy call will we make answer; thine Apostles will we follow." "Did ye not once swear that no change should befal you?

records.label: Surah 14 · edition paragraph 48
records.text: Yet ye dwelt in the dwellings of those6 who were the authors of their undoing7 and it was made plain to you how we had dealt with them; and we held them up to you as examples. They plotted their plots: but God could master their plots, even though their plots had been so powerful as to move the mountains."

records.label: Surah 14 · edition paragraph 49
records.text: Think not then that God will fail his promise to his Apostles: aye! God is mighty, and Vengeance is His.

records.label: Surah 14 · edition paragraph 50
records.text: On the day when the Earth shall be changed into another Earth, and the Heavens also, men shall come forth unto God, the Only, the Victorious.

records.label: Surah 14 · edition paragraph 51
records.text: And thou shalt see the wicked on that day linked together in chains-

records.label: Surah 14 · edition paragraph 52
records.text: Their garments of pitch, and fire shall enwrap their faces that God may reward every soul as it deserveth; verily God is prompt to reckon.

records.label: Surah 14 · edition paragraph 53
records.text: This is a message for mankind, that they may thereby be warned: and that they may know that there is but one God; and that men of understanding may ponder it.

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 1
records.text: In the Name of God, the Compassionate, the Merciful

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 2
records.text: ELIF. LAM. RA.2 These are the signs of the Book, and of a lucid recital [Koran].

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 3
records.text: Many a time will the infidels wish that they had been Muslims.

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 4
records.text: Let them feast and enjoy themselves, and let hope beguile them: but they shall know the truth at last.

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 5
records.text: We never destroyed a city whose term was not perfixed:3

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 6
records.text: No people can forestall or retard its destiny.

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 7
records.text: They say: "O thou to whom the warning hath been sent down, thou art surely possessed by a djinn:

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 8
records.text: Wouldst thou not have come to us with the angels, if thou wert of those who assert the truth?"

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 9
records.text: -We will not send down the angels without due cause.4 The Infidels would not in that case have been respited.

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 10
records.text: Verily, We have sent down the warning, and verily, We will be its guardian;

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 11
records.text: And already have We sent Apostles, before thee, among the sects of the ancients;

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 12
records.text: But never came Apostles to them whom they did not deride.

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 13
records.text: In like manner will We put it into the hearts of the sinners of Mecca to do the same:

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 14
records.text: They will not believe on him though the example of those of old hath gone before.

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 15
records.text: Even were We to open above them a gate in Heaven, yet all the while they were mounting up to it,

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 16
records.text: They would surely say: It is only that our eyes are drunken: nay, we are a people enchanted.

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 17
records.text: We have set the signs of the zodiac5 in the Heavens, and adorned and decked them forth for the beholders,

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 18
records.text: And We guard them from every stoned6 Satan,

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 19
records.text: Save such as steal a hearing:7 and him doth a visible flame pursue.

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 20
records.text: And the Earth have We spread forth, and thrown thereon the mountains, and caused everything to spring forth in it in balanced measure:

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 21
records.text: And We have provided therein sustenance for you, and for the creatures which not ye sustain:

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 22
records.text: And no one thing is there, but with Us are its storehouses; and We send it not down but in settled measure:

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 23
records.text: And We send forth the fertilising winds, and cause the rain to come down from the heaven, and give you to drink of it; and it is not ye who are its storers:

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 24
records.text: And We cause to live and We cause to die,8 and We are the heir of all things:

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 25
records.text: We know those of you who flourish first and We know those who come later:

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 26
records.text: And truly thy Lord will gather them together again, for He is Wise, Knowing.

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 27
records.text: We created man of dried clay, of dark loam moulded;

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 28
records.text: And the djinn had We before created of subtle fire.

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 29
records.text: Remember when thy Lord said to the Angels, "I create man of dried clay, of dark loam moulded:

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 30
records.text: And when I shall have fashioned him and breathed of my spirit into him, then fall ye down and worship him."

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 31
records.text: And the Angels bowed down in worship, all of them, all together,

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 32
records.text: Save Eblis: he refused to be with those who bowed in worship.

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 33
records.text: "O Eblis,"9 said God, "wherefore art thou not with those who bow down in worship?"

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 34
records.text: He said, "It beseemeth not me to bow in worship to man whom thou hast created of clay, of moulded loam."

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 35
records.text: He said, "Begone then hence; thou art a stoned one,10

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 36
records.text: And the curse shall be on thee till the day of reckoning."

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 37
records.text: He said, "O my Lord! respite me till the day when man shall be raised from the dead."

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 38
records.text: He said, "One then of the respited shalt thou be

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 39
records.text: Till the day of the predestined time."

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 40
records.text: He said, "O my Lord! because thou hast beguiled me, I will surely make all fair seeming to them11 on the earth; I will surely beguile them all;

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 41
records.text: Except such of them as shall be thy sincere servants."

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 42
records.text: He said, "This is the right way with me;

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 43
records.text: For over none of my servants shalt thou have power, save those beguiled ones who shall follow thee."

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 44
records.text: And verily, Hell is the promise for them one and all.

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 45
records.text: It hath seven Portals;12 at each Portal is a separate band of them;

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 46
records.text: But 'mid gardens and fountains shall the pious dwell:

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 47
records.text: "Enter ye therein in peace, secure-"

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 48
records.text: And all rancour will We remove from their bosoms: they shall sit as brethren, face to face, on couches:

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 49
records.text: Therein no weariness shall reach them, nor forth from it shall they be cast for ever.

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 50
records.text: Announce to my servants that I am the Gracious, the Merciful,

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 51
records.text: And that my chastisement is the grievous chastisement.

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 52
records.text: And tell them of Abraham's guests.

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 53
records.text: When they entered in unto him, and said, "Peace."

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 54
records.text: "Verily," said he, "We fear you."

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 55
records.text: They said, "Fear not, for of a sage son we bring thee tidings."

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 56
records.text: He said, "Bring ye me such tidings now that old age hath come upon me? What, therefore, are your tidings really?"

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 57
records.text: They said, "We announce them to thee in very truth. Be not then one of the despairing."

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 58
records.text: "And who," said he, "despaireth of the mercy of his Lord, but they who err?"

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 59
records.text: He said, "What is your business then, O ye Sent Ones?"

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 60
records.text: They said, "We are sent unto a people who are sinners,

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 61
records.text: Except the family of Lot, whom verily we will rescue all,

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 62
records.text: Except his wife. We have decreed that she shall be of those who linger."

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 63
records.text: And when the Sent Ones came to the family of Lot

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 64
records.text: He said, "Yes; are persons unknown to me."

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 65
records.text: They said, "Yes; but we have come to thee for a purpose about which thy people doubt:

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 66
records.text: We have come to thee with very truth, and we are truthful envoys.

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 67
records.text: Lead forth therefore thy family in the dead of the night; follow thou on their rear: and let no one of you turn round, but pass ye on whither ye are bidden."

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 68
records.text: And this command we gave him because to the last man should these people be cut off at morning.

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 69
records.text: Then came the people of the city rejoicing at the news13-

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 70
records.text: He said, "These are my guests: therefore disgrace me not.

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 71
records.text: And fear God and put me not to shame."

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 72
records.text: They said, "Have we not forbidden thee to entertain any one whatever?"14

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 73
records.text: He said, "Here are my daughters, if ye will thus act."

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 74
records.text: As thou livest, O Muhammad, they were bewildered in the drunkenness of their lust.

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 75
records.text: So a tempest overtook them at their sunrise,

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 76
records.text: And we turned the city upside down, and we rained stones of baked clay upon them.

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 77
records.text: Verily, in this are signs for those who scan heedfully;

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 78
records.text: And these cities lay on the high road.15

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 79
records.text: Verily, in this are signs for the faithful.

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 80
records.text: The inhabitants also of El Aika16 were sinners:

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 81
records.text: So we took vengeance on them, and they both became a plain example.

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 82
records.text: And the people of HEDJR treated God's messengers as liars.

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 83
records.text: And we brought forth our signs to them, but they drew back from them:

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 84
records.text: And they hewed them out abodes in the mountains to secure them:

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 85
records.text: But a tempest surprised them at early morn,

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 86
records.text: And their labours availed them nothing.

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 87
records.text: We have not created the heavens and the earth and all that between them is, but for a worthy end.17 And verily, "the hour" shall surely come. Wherefore do thou, Muhammad, forgive with kindly forgiveness,

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 88
records.text: For thy Lord! He is the Creator, the Wise.

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 89
records.text: We have already given thee the seven verses of repetition18 and the glorious Koran.

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 90
records.text: Strain not thine eyes after the good things we have bestowed on some of the unbelievers: afflict not thyself on their account, and lower thy wing to the faithful.19

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 91
records.text: And SAY: I am the only plain-spoken warner.

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 92
records.text: We will punish those who foster divisions,20

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 93
records.text: Who break up the Koran into parts:

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 94
records.text: By thy Lord! we will surely take account from them one and all,

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 95
records.text: Concerning that which they have done.

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 96
records.text: Profess publicly then what thou hast been bidden,21 and withdraw from those who join gods to God.

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 97
records.text: Verily, We will maintain thy cause against those who deride thee,

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 98
records.text: Who set up gods with God: and at last shall they know their folly.

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 99
records.text: Now know We that thy heart is distressed22 at what they say:

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 100
records.text: But do thou celebrate the praise of thy Lord, and be of those who bow down in worship;

records.label: Surah 15 · edition paragraph 101
records.text: And serve thy Lord till the certainty23 o'ertake thee.

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 1
records.text: In the Name of God, the Compassionate, the Merciful

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 2
records.text: THE doom of God cometh to pass. Then hasten it not. Glory be to Him! High let Him be exalted above the gods whom they join with Him!

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 3
records.text: By his own behest will He cause the angels to descend with the Spirit on whom he pleaseth among his servants, bidding them, "Warn that there is no God but me; therefore fear me."

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 4
records.text: He hath created the Heavens and the Earth to set forth his truth;1 high let Him be exalted above the gods they join with Him!

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 5
records.text: Man hath He created from a moist germ;2 yet lo! man is an open caviller.

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 6
records.text: And the cattle! for you hath He created them: in them ye have warm garments and gainful uses; and of them ye eat:

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 7
records.text: And they beseem you well3 when ye fetch them home and when ye drive them forth to pasture:

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 8
records.text: And they carry your burdens to lands which ye could not else reach but with travail of soul: truly your Lord is full of goodness, and merciful:

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 9
records.text: And He hath given you horses, mules, and asses, that ye may ride them, and for your ornament: and things of which ye have no knowledge hath he created.

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 10
records.text: Of God it is to point out "the Way." Some turn aside from it: but had He pleased, He had guided you all aright.

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 11
records.text: It is He who sendeth down rain out of Heaven: from it is your drink; and from it are the plants by which ye pasture.

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 12
