records.text: By it He causeth the corn, and the olives, and the palm-trees, and the grapes to spring forth for you, and all kinds of fruits: verily, in this are signs for those who ponder.

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 13
records.text: And He hath subjected to you the night and the day; the sun and the moon and the stars too are subjected to you by his behest; verily, in this are signs for those who understand:

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 14
records.text: And all of varied hues that He hath created for you over the earth: verily, in this are signs for those who remember.

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 15
records.text: And He it is who hath subjected the sea to you, that ye may eat of its fresh fish, and take forth from it ornaments to wear-thou seest the ships ploughing its billows-and that ye may go in quest of his bounties, and that ye might give thanks.

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 16
records.text: And He hath thrown firm mountains on the earth, least it move with you; and rivers and paths for your guidance,

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 17
records.text: And way marks. By the stars too are men guided.

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 18
records.text: Shall He then who hath created be as he who hath not created? Will ye not consider?

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 19
records.text: And if ye would reckon up the favours of God, ye could not count them. Aye! God is right Gracious, Merciful!

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 20
records.text: And God knoweth what ye conceal, and what ye bring to light,

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 21
records.text: While the gods whom they call on beside God, create nothing, but are themselves created:

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 22
records.text: Dead are they, lifeless! and they know not

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 23
records.text: When they shall be raised!

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 24
records.text: Your God is the one God: and they who believe not in a future life, have hearts given to denial, and are men of pride:-

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 25
records.text: Beyond a doubt God knoweth what they conceal and what they manifest:-

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 26
records.text: He truly loveth not the men of pride.

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 27
records.text: For when it is said to them, "What is this your Lord hath sent down?" they say, "Fables of the ancients,"-

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 28
records.text: That on the day of resurrection they may bear their own entire burden, and the burden of those whom they, in their ignorance, misled. Shall it not be a grievous burden for them?

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 29
records.text: They who were before them did plot of old. But God attacked their building at its foundation the roof fell on them from above; and, whence they looked not for it, punishment overtook them:4

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 30
records.text: On the day of resurrection, too, will He shame them. He will say, "Where are the gods ye associated with me, the subjects of your disputes?" They to whom "the knowledge" hath been given will say, Verily, this day shall shame and evil fall upon the infidels.

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 31
records.text: The sinners against their own souls whom the angels shall cause to die will proffer the submission, "No evil have we done." Nay! God knoweth what ye have wrought:

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 32
records.text: Enter ye therefore the gates of Hell to remain therein for ever: and horrid the abiding place of the haughty ones!

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 33
records.text: But to those who have feared God it shall be said, "What is this that your Lord hath awarded?" They shall say, "That which is best. To those who do good, a good reward in this present world; but better the mansion of the next, and right pleasant the abode of the God-fearing!"

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 34
records.text: Gardens of Eden into which they shall enter; rivers shall flow beneath their shades; all they wish for shall they find therein! Thus God rewardeth those who fear Him;

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 35
records.text: To whom, as righteous persons, the angels shall say, when they receive their souls, "Peace be on you! Enter Paradise as the meed of your labours."

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 36
records.text: What can the infidels expect but that the angels of death come upon them, or that a sentence of thy Lord take effect? Thus did they who flourished before them. God was not unjust to them, but to their ownselves were they unjust;

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 37
records.text: And the ill which they had done recoiled upon them, and that which they had scoffed at encompassed them round about.

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 38
records.text: They who have joined other gods with God say, "Had He pleased, neither we nor our fathers had worshipped aught but him; nor should we, apart from him, have forbidden aught." Thus acted they who were before them. Yet is the duty of the apostles other than public preaching?

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 39
records.text: And to every people have we sent an apostle saying:-Worship God and turn away from Taghout.5 Some of them there were whom God guided, and there were others decreed to err. But go through the land and see what hath been the end of those who treated my apostles as liars!

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 40
records.text: If thou art anxious for their guidance, know that God will not guide him whom He would lead astray, neither shall they have any helpers.

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 41
records.text: And they swear by God with their most sacred oath that "God will never raise him who once is dead." Nay, but on Him is a promise binding, though most men know it not,-

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 42
records.text: That He may clear up to them the subject of their disputes, and that the infidels may know that they are liars.

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 43
records.text: Our word to a thing when we will it, is but to say, "Be," and it is.6

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 44
records.text: And as to those who when oppressed have fled their country for the sake of God, we will surely provide them a goodly abode in this world, but greater the reward of the next life, did they but know it

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 45
records.text: They who bear ills with patience and put their trust in the Lord!

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 46
records.text: None have we sent before thee but men inspired ask of those who have Books of Monition,7 if ye know it not-

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 47
records.text: With proofs of their mission and Scriptures: and to thee have we sent down this Book of Monition that thou mayest make clear to men what hath been sent down to them, and that they may ponder it.

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 48
records.text: What! Are they then who have plotted mischiefs, sure that God will not cause the earth to cleave under them? or that a chastisement will not come upon them whence they looked not for it?

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 49
records.text: Or that He will not seize upon them in their comings and goings, while they shall not be able to resist him?

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 50
records.text: Or that he will not seize them with some slowly wasting scourge? But verily your Lord is Good, Gracious.

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 51
records.text: Have they not seen how everything which God hath created turneth its shadow right and left, prostrating itself before God in all abasement?

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 52
records.text: And all in the Heavens and all on the Earth, each thing that moveth, and the very angels, prostrate them in adoration before God, and are free from pride;

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 53
records.text: They fear their Lord who is above them, and do what they are bidden:

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 54
records.text: For God hath said, "Take not to yourselves two gods, for He is one God: me, therefore! yea, me revere!

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 55
records.text: All in the Heavens and in the Earth is His! His due unceasing service! Will ye then fear any other than God?

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 56
records.text: And all your blessings are assuredly from God: then, when trouble befalleth you, to Him ye turn for help:

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 57
records.text: Then when He relieveth you of the trouble, lo! some of you join associates with your Lord:-

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 58
records.text: To prove how thankless are they for our gifts! Enjoy yourselves then: but in the end ye shall know the truth.

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 59
records.text: And for idols, of which they know nothing, they set apart a share of our bounties! By God ye shall be called to account for your devices!

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 60
records.text: And they ascribe daughters unto God! Glory be to Him! But they desire them not for themselves:8

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 61
records.text: For when the birth of a daughter is announced to any one of them, dark shadows settle on his face, and he is sad:

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 62
records.text: He hideth him from the people because of the ill tidings: shall he keep it with disgrace or bury it in the dust?9 Are not their judgments wrong?

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 63
records.text: To whatever is evil may they be likened who believe not in a future life;10 but God is to be likened to whatever is loftiest: for He is the Mighty, the Wise.

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 64
records.text: Should God punish men for their perverse doings, he would not leave on earth a moving thing! but to an appointed term doth He respite them; and when their term is come, they shall not delay or advance it an hour.

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 65
records.text: Yet what they loathe themselves do they assign to God; and their tongues utter the lie, that theirs shall be a goodly lot. But beyond a doubt is it that the fire awaiteth them, and that they shall be the first sent into it.

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 66
records.text: By God we have sent Apostles to nations before thee, but Satan prepared their work for them, and this day is he their liege; and a woeful punishment doth await them.

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 67
records.text: And we have sent down the Book to thee only, that thou mightest clear up to them the subject of their wranglings, and as a guidance and a mercy to those who believe.

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 68
records.text: And God sendeth down water from Heaven, and by it giveth life to the Earth after it hath been dead: verily, in this is a sign to those who hearken.

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 69
records.text: Ye have also teaching from the cattle. We give you drink of the pure milk, between dregs and blood, which is in their bellies; the pleasant beverage of them that quaff it.

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 70
records.text: And among fruits ye have the palm and the vine, from which ye get wine and healthful nutriment: in this, verily, are signs for those who reflect.

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 71
records.text: And thy Lord hath taught the BEE, saying: "Provide thee houses in the mountains, and in the trees, and in the hives which men do build thee:

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 72
records.text: Feed, moreover, on every kind of fruit, and walk the beaten paths of thy Lord." From its belly cometh forth a fluid of varying hues,11 which yieldeth medicine to man. Verily in this is a sign for those who consider.

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 73
records.text: And God hath created you; by and bye will he take you to himself; and some among you will he carry on to abject old age, when all that once was known is known no longer. Aye, God is Knowing, Powerful.

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 74
records.text: And God hath abounded to some of you more than to others in the supplies of life; yet they to whom He hath abounded, impart not thereof to the slaves whom their right hands possess, so that they may share alike. What! will they deny, then, that these boons are from God?

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 75
records.text: God, too, hath given you wives of your own race, and from your wives hath He given you sons and grandsons, and with good things hath he supplied you. What, will they then believe in vain idols? For God's boons they are ungrateful!

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 76
records.text: And they worship beside God those who neither out of the Heavens or Earth can provide them a particle of food, and have no power in themselves!

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 77
records.text: Make no comparisons, therefore, with God.12 Verily, God hath knowledge, but ye have not.

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 78
records.text: God maketh comparison between a slave13 the property of his lord, who hath no power over anything, and a free man whom we have ourselves supplies, and who giveth alms therefrom both in secret and openly. Shall they be held equal? No: praise be to God! But most men know it not.

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 79
records.text: God setteth forth also a comparison between two men, one of whom is dumb from his birth, and hath no power over anything, and is a burden to his lord: send him where he will, he cometh not back with success. Shall he and the man who enjoineth what is just, and keepeth in the straight path, be held equal?

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 80
records.text: God's are the secrets of the Heavens and of the Earth! and the business of the last hour will be but as the twinkling of an eye, or even less. Yes! for all things is God Potent.

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 81
records.text: God hath brought you out of your mothers' wombs devoid of all knowledge; but hath given you hearing, and sight, and heart, that haply ye might render thanks.

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 82
records.text: Have they never looked up at the birds subjected to Him in Heaven's vault? None holdeth them in hand but God! In this are signs for those who believe.

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 83
records.text: And God hath given you tents to dwell in: and He hath given you the skins of beasts for tents, that ye may find them light when ye shift your quarters, or when ye halt; and from their wool and soft fur and hair, hath He supplied you with furniture and goods for temporary use.

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 84
records.text: And from the things which He hath created, hath God provided shade for you, and hath given you the mountains for places of shelter, and hath given you garments to defend you from the heat, and garments to defend you in your wars. Thus doth He fill up the measure of His goodness towards you, that you may resign yourselves to Him.

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 85
records.text: But if they turn their backs, still thy office is only plain spoken preaching.

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 86
records.text: They own the goodness of God-then they disown it-and most of them are infidels.

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 87
records.text: But one day, we will raise up a witness out of every nation: them shall the infidels have no permission to make excuses, and they shall find no favour.

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 88
records.text: And when they who have acted thus wrongly shall behold their torment, it shall not be made light to them, nor will God deign to look upon them.

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 89
records.text: And when they who had joined associates with God shall see those their associate-gods, they shall say, "O our Lord! these are our associate-gods whom we called upon beside Thee." But they shall retort on them, "Verily, ye are liars."

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 90
records.text: And on that day shall they proffer submission to God; and the deities of their own invention shall vanish from them.

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 91
records.text: As for those who were infidels and turned others aside from the way of God, to them we will add punishment on punishment for their corrupt doings.

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 92
records.text: And one day we will summon up in every people a witness against them from among themselves; and we will bring thee up as a witness against these Meccans: for to thee have we sent down the Book which cleareth up everything, a guidance, and mercy, and glad tidings to those who resign themselves to God (to Muslims).

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 93
records.text: Verily, God enjoineth justice and the doing of good and gifts to kindred, and he forbiddeth wickedness and wrong and oppression. He warneth you that haply ye may be mindful.

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 94
records.text: Be faithful in the covenant of God when ye have covenanted, and break not your oaths after ye have pledged them: for now have ye made God to stand surety for you. Verily, God hath knowledge of what ye do.

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 95
records.text: And, because you are a more numerous people than some other people, be not like her who unravelleth the thread which she had strongly spun, by taking your oaths with mutual perfidy. God is making trial of you in this: and in the day of resurrection he will assuredly clear up to you that concerning which ye are now at variance.

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 96
records.text: Had God pleased, He could have made you one people: but He causeth whom He will to err, and whom He will He guideth: and ye shall assuredly be called to account for your doings.

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 97
records.text: Therefore take not your oaths with mutual fraud, lest your foot slip after it hath been firmly fixed, and ye taste of evil because ye have turned others aside from the way of God, and great be your punishment.

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 98
records.text: And barter not the covenant of God for a mean price; for with God is that which is better for you, if ye do but understand.

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 99
records.text: All that is with you passeth away, but that which is with God abideth. With a reward meet for their best deeds will we surely recompense those who have patiently endured.

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 100
records.text: Whoso doeth that which is right, whether male or female, if a believer, him will we surely quicken to a happy life, and recompense them with a reward meet for their best deeds.

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 101
records.text: When thou readest the Koran, have recourse to God for help against Satan the stoned,14

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 102
records.text: For no power hath he over those who believe, and put their trust in their Lord,

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 103
records.text: But only hath he power over those who turn away from God, and join other deities with Him.

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 104
records.text: And when we change one (sign) verse for another, and God knoweth best what He revealeth, they say, "Thou art only a fabricator." Nay! but most of them have no knowledge.

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 105
records.text: SAY: The Holy Spirit15 hath brought it down with truth from thy Lord, that He may stablish those who have believed, and as guidance and glad tidings to the Muslims.

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 106
records.text: We also know that they say, "Surely a certain person teacheth him." But the tongue of him at whom they hint is foreign,16 while this Koran is in the plain Arabic.

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 107
records.text: As for those who believe not in the signs of God, God will not guide them, and a sore torment doth await them.

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 108
records.text: Surely they invent a lie who believe not in the signs of God-and they are the liars.

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 109
records.text: Whoso, after he hath believed in God denieth him, if he were forced to it and if his heart remain steadfast in the faith, shall be guiltless:17 but whoso openeth his breast to infidelity-on such shall be wrath from God, and a severe punishment awaiteth them.

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 110
records.text: This, because they have loved this present life beyond the next, and because God guideth not the unbelievers!

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 111
records.text: These are they whose hearts and ears and eyes God hath sealed up: these are the careless ones: in the next world shall they perish beyond a doubt.

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 112
records.text: To those also who after their trials fled their country,18 then fought and endured with patience, verily, thy Lord will in the end be forgiving, gracious.

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 113
records.text: On a certain day shall every soul come to plead for itself, and every soul shall be repaid according to its deeds; and they shall not be wronged.

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 114
records.text: God proposeth the instance of a city,19 secure and at ease, to which its supplies come in plenty from every side. But she was thankless for the boons of God; God therefore made her taste the woe20 of famine and of fear, for what they had done.

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 115
records.text: Moreover, an apostle of their own people came to them, and they treated him as an impostor. So chastisement overtook them because they were evil doers.

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 116
records.text: Of what God hath supplied you eat the lawful and good, and be grateful for the favours of God, if ye are his worshippers.

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 117
records.text: Forbidden to you is that only which dieth of itself, and blood, and swine's flesh, and that which hath been slain in the name of any other than God: but if any be forced, and neither lust for it nor wilfully transgress, then verily God is forgiving, gracious.21

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 118
records.text: And say not with a lie upon your tongue, "This is lawful and this is forbidden:" for so will ye invent a lie concerning God: but they who invent a lie of God shall not prosper:

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 119
records.text: Brief their enjoyment, but sore their punishment!

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 120
records.text: To the Jews22 we have forbidden that of which we before told thee; we injured them not, but they injured themselves.

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 121
records.text: To those who have done evil in ignorance, then afterwards have repented and amended, verily thy Lord is in the end right gracious, merciful.

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 122
records.text: Verily, Abraham was a leader in religion:23 obedient to God, sound in faith:24 he was not of those who join gods with God.

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 123
records.text: Grateful was he for His favours: God chose him and guided him into the straight way;

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 124
records.text: And we bestowed on him good things in this world: and in the world to come he shall be among the just.

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 125
records.text: We have moreover revealed to thee that thou follow the religion of Abraham, the sound in faith. He was not of those who join gods with God.

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 126
records.text: The Sabbath was only ordained for those who differed about it: and of a truth thy Lord will decide between them on the day of resurrection as to the subject of their disputes.

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 127
records.text: Summon thou to the way of thy Lord with wisdom and with kindly warning: dispute with them in the kindest manner: thy Lord best knoweth those who stray from his way, and He best knoweth those who have yielded to his guidance.

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 128
records.text: If ye make reprisals,25 then make them to the same extent that ye were injured: but if ye can endure patiently, best will it be for the patiently enduring.

records.label: Surah 16 · edition paragraph 129
records.text: Endure then with patience. But thy patient endurance must be sought in none but God. And be not grieved about the infidels, and be not troubled at their devices; for God is with those who fear him and do good deeds.

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 1
records.text: In the Name of God, the Compassionate, the Merciful

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 2
records.text: GLORY be to Him who carried his servant by night2 from the sacred temple of Mecca to the temple3 that is more remote, whose precinct we have blessed, that we might shew him of our signs! for He is the Hearer, the Seer.

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 3
records.text: And4 we gave the Book to Moses and ordained it for guidance to the children of Israel-"that ye take no other Guardian than me."

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 4
records.text: O posterity of those whom we bare with Noah! He truly was a grateful servant!

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 5
records.text: And we solemnly declared to the children of Israel in the Book, "Twice surely will ye enact crimes in the earth, and with great loftiness of pride will ye surely be uplifted."

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 6
records.text: So when the menace for the first crime5 came to be inflicted, we sent against you our servants endued with terrible prowess; and they searched the inmost part of your abodes, and the menace was accomplished.

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 7
records.text: Then we gave you the mastery over them6 in turn, and increased you in wealth and children, and made you a most numerous host.

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 8
records.text: We said, "If ye do well, to your own behoof will ye do well: and if ye do evil, against yourselves will ye do it. And when the menace for your latter crime7 came to be inflicted, then we sent an enemy to sadden your faces, and to enter the temple as they entered it at first, and to destroy with utter destruction that which they had conquered.

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 9
records.text: Haply your Lord will have mercy on you! but if ye return, we will return:8 and we have appointed Hell-the prison of the infidels.

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 10
records.text: Verily, this Koran guideth to what is most upright; and it announceth to believers

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 11
records.text: Who do the things that are right, that for them is a great reward;

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 12
records.text: And that for those who believe not in the life to come, we have got ready a painful punishment.

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 13
records.text: Man prayeth for evil as he prayeth for good; for man is hasty.

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 14
records.text: We have made the night and the day for two signs: the sign of the night do we obscure, but the sign of the day cause we to shine forth, that ye may seek plenty from your Lord, and that ye may know the number of the years and the reckoning of time; and we have made everything distinct by distinctiveness.

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 15
records.text: And every man's fate9 have we fastened about his neck: and on the day of resurrection will we bring forth to him a book which shall be proffered to him wide open:

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 16
records.text: -"Read thy Book:10 there needeth none but thyself to make out an account against thee this day."

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 17
records.text: For his own good only shall the guided yield to guidance, and to his own loss only shall the erring err; and the heavy laden shall not be laden with another's load. We never punished until we had first sent an apostle:

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 18
records.text: And when we willed to destroy a city, to its affluent ones did we address our bidding; but when they acted criminally therein, just was its doom, and we destroyed it with an utter destruction.

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 19
records.text: And since Noah, how many nations have we exterminated! And of the sins of his servants thy Lord is sufficiently informed, observant.

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 20
records.text: Whoso chooseth this quickly passing life, quickly will we bestow therein that which we please-even on him we choose; afterward we will appoint hell for him, in which he shall burn-disgraced, outcast:

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 21
records.text: But whoso chooseth the next life, and striveth after it as it should be striven for, being also a believer,-these! their striving shall be grateful to God:

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 22
records.text: To all-both to these and those-will we prolong the gifts of thy Lord; for not to any shall the gifts of thy Lord be denied.

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 23
records.text: See how we have caused some of them to excel others! but the next life shall be greater in its grades, and greater in excellence.

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 24
records.text: Set not up another god with God, lest thou sit thee down disgraced, helpless.11

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 25
records.text: Thy Lord hath ordained that ye worship none but him; and, kindness to your parents, whether one or both of them attain to old age with thee: and say not to them, "Fie!" neither reproach them; but speak to them both with respectful speech;

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 26
records.text: And defer humbly to them12 out of tenderness; and say, "Lord, have compassion on them both, even as they reared me when I was little."

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 27
records.text: Your Lord well knoweth what is in your souls; he knoweth whether ye be righteous:

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 28
records.text: And gracious is He to those who return to Him.

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 29
records.text: And to him who is of kin render his due, and also to the poor and to the wayfarer; yet waste not wastefully,

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 30
records.text: For the wasteful are brethren of the Satans, and Satan was ungrateful to his Lord:

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 31
records.text: But if thou turn away from them, while thou thyself seekest boons from thy Lord for which thou hopest, at least speak to them with kindly speech:

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 32
records.text: And let not thy hand be tied up to thy neck; nor yet open it with all openness, lest thou sit thee down in rebuke, in beggary.

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 33
records.text: Verily, thy Lord will provide with open hand for whom he pleaseth, and will be sparing. His servants doth he scan, inspect.

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 34
records.text: Kill not your children for fear of want:13 for them and for you will we provide. Verily, the killing them is a great wickedness.

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 35
records.text: Have nought to do with adultery; for it is a foul thing and an evil way:

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 36
records.text: Neither slay any one whom God hath forbidden you to slay, unless for a just cause: and whosoever shall be slain wrongfully, to his heir14 have we given powers; but let him not outstep bounds in putting the manslayer to death, for he too, in his turn, will be assisted and avenged.

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 37
records.text: And touch not the substance of the orphan, unless in an upright way, till he attain his age of strength: And perform your covenant; verily the covenant shall be enquired of:

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 38
records.text: And give full measure when you measure, and weigh with just balance. This will be better, and fairest for settlement:

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 39
records.text: And follow not that of which thou hast no knowledge;15 because the hearing and the sight and the heart,-each of these shall be enquired of:

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 40
records.text: And walk not proudly on the earth, for thou canst not cleave the earth, neither shalt thou reach to the mountains in height:

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 41
records.text: All this is evil; odious to thy Lord.

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 42
records.text: This is a part of the wisdom which thy Lord hath revealed to thee. Set not up any other god with God, lest thou be cast into Hell, rebuked, cast away.

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 43
records.text: What! hath your Lord prepared sons for you, and taken for himself daughters from among the angels? Indeed, ye say a dreadful saying.

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 44
records.text: Moreover, for man's warning have we varied16 this Koran: Yet it only increaseth their flight from it.

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 45
records.text: SAY: If, as ye affirm, there were other gods with Him, they would in that case seek occasion against the occupant of the throne:

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 46
records.text: Glory to Him! Immensely high is He exalted above their blasphemies!

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 47
records.text: The seven heavens17 praise him, and the earth, and all who are therein; neither is there aught which doth not celebrate his praise; but their utterances of praise ye understand not. He is kind, indulgent.

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 48
records.text: When thou recitest the Koran we place between thee and those who believe not in the life to come, a dark veil;

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 49
records.text: And we put coverings over their hearts lest they should understand it, and in their ears a heaviness;

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 50
records.text: And when in the Koran thou namest thy One Lord, they turn their backs in flight.

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 51
records.text: We well know why they hearken, when they hearken unto thee, and when they whisper apart; when the wicked say, "Ye follow no other than a man enchanted."

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 52
records.text: See what likenesses they strike out for thee! But they are in error, neither can they find the path.

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 53
records.text: They also say, "After we shall have become bones and dust, shall we in sooth be raised a new creation?"

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 54
records.text: SAY: "Yes, though ye were stones, or iron, or any other creature, to your seeming, yet harder to be raised." But they will say, "Who shall bring us back?" SAY: "He who created you at first." And they will wag their heads at thee, and say, "When shall this be?" SAY: "Haply it is nigh."

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 55
records.text: On that day shall God call you forth, and ye shall answer by praising Him; and ye shall seem to have tarried but a little while.

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 56
records.text: Enjoin my servants to speak in kindly sort: Verily Satan would stir up strifes among them, for Satan is man's avowed foe.

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 57
records.text: Your Lord well knoweth you: if He please He will have mercy on you; or if He please He will chastise you: and we have not sent thee to be a guardian over them.

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 58
records.text: Thy Lord hath full knowledge of all in the heavens and the earth. Higher gifts have we given to some of the prophets than to others, and the Psalter we gave to David.

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 59
records.text: SAY: Call ye upon those whom ye fancy to be gods beside Him; yet they will have no power to relieve you from trouble, or to shift it elsewhere.

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 60
records.text: Those whom ye call on, themselves desire union with their Lord,18 striving which of them shall be nearest to him: they also hope for his mercy and fear his chastisement. Verily the chastisement of thy Lord is to be dreaded.

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 61
records.text: There is no city which we will not destroy before the day of Resurrection, or chastise it with a grievous chastisement. This is written in the Book.

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 62
records.text: Nothing hindered us from sending thee with the power of working miracles, except that the peoples of old treated them as lies. We gave to Themoud19 the she-camel before their very eyes, yet they maltreated her! We send not a prophet with miracles but to strike terror.

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 63
records.text: And remember when we said to thee, Verily, thy Lord is round about mankind; we ordained the vision20 which we shewed thee, and likewise the cursed tree of the Koran, only for men to dispute of; we will strike them with terror; but it shall only increase in them enormous wickedness:

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 64
records.text: And when we said to the Angels, "Prostrate yourselves before Adam:" and they all prostrated them, save Eblis. "What!" said he, "shall I bow me before him whom thou hast created of clay?

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 65
records.text: Seest thou this man whom thou hast honoured above me? Verily, if thou respite me till the day of Resurrection, I will destroy his offspring, except a few."

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 66
records.text: He said, "Begone; but whosoever of them shall follow thee, verily, Hell shall be your recompense; an ample recompense!

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 67
records.text: And entice such of them as thou canst by thy voice; assault them with thy horsemen and thy footmen;21 be their partner in their riches and in their children, and make them promises: but Satan shall make them only deceitful promises.

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 68
records.text: As to my servants, no power over them shalt thou have; And thy Lord will be their sufficient guardian."

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 69
records.text: It is your Lord who speedeth onward the ships for you in the sea, that ye may seek of his abundance; for he is merciful towards you.

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 70
records.text: When a misfortune befalleth you out at sea, they whom ye invoke are not to be found: God alone is there: yet when he bringeth you safe to dry land, ye place yourselves at a distance from Him. Ungrateful is man.

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 71
records.text: What! are ye sure, then, that he will not cleave the sides of the earth for you? or that he will not send against you a whirlwind charged with sands? Then shall ye find no protector.

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 72
records.text: Or are ye sure that he will not cause you to put back to sea a second time, and send against you a storm blast, and drown you, for that ye have been thankless? Then shall ye find no helper against us therein.

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 73
records.text: And now have we honoured the children of Adam: by land and by sea have we carried them: food have we provided for them of good things, and with endowments beyond many of our creatures have we endowed them.

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 74
records.text: One day we will summon all men with their leaders: they whose book shall be given into their right hand, shall read their book, and not be wronged a thread:

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 75
records.text: And he who has been blind here, shall be blind hereafter, and wander yet more from the way.

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 76
records.text: And, verily, they had well nigh beguiled thee from what we revealed to thee, and caused thee to invent some other thing in our name: but in that case they would surely have taken thee as a friend;22

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 77
records.text: And had we not settled thee, thou hadst well nigh leaned to them a little:

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 78
records.text: In that case we would surely have made thee taste of woe23 in life and of woe in death: then thou shouldest not have found a helper against us.

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 79
records.text: And truly they had almost caused thee to quit the land, in order wholly to drive thee forth from it:24 but then, themselves should have tarried but a little after thee.

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 80
records.text: This was our way with the Apostles we have already sent before thee, and in this our way thou shalt find no change.

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 81
records.text: Observe prayer at sunset, till the first darkening of the night, and the daybreak reading-for the daybreak reading hath its witnesses,

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 82
records.text: And watch unto it in the night: this shall be an excess in service:25 it may be that thy Lord will raise thee to a glorious station:

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 83
records.text: And say, "O my Lord, cause me to enter26 with a perfect entry, and to come forth with a perfect forthcoming, and give me from thy presence a helping power:"

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 84
records.text: And SAY: Truth is come and falsehood is vanished. Verily, falsehood is a thing that vanisheth.

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 85
records.text: And we send down of the Koran that which is a healing and a mercy to the faithful: But it shall only add to the ruin of the wicked.

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 86
records.text: When we bestow favours on man, he withdraweth and goeth aside; but when evil toucheth him, he is despairing.

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 87
records.text: SAY: Every one acteth after his own manner: but your Lord well knoweth who is best guided in his path.

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 88
records.text: And they will ask thee of the Spirit.27 SAY: The Spirit proceedeth at my Lord's command: but of knowledge, only a little to you is given.

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 89
records.text: If we pleased, we could take away what we have revealed to thee: none couldst thou then find thee to undertake thy cause with us,

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 90
records.text: Save as a mercy from thy Lord; great, verily, is his favour towards thee.

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 91
records.text: SAY: Verily, were men and Djinn assembled to produce the like of this Koran, they could not produce its like, though the one should help the other.

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 92
records.text: And of a truth we have set out to men every kind of similitude in this Koran, but most men have refused everything except unbelief.

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 93
records.text: And they say, "By no means will we believe on thee till thou cause a fountain to gush forth for us from the earth;

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 94
records.text: Or, till thou have a garden of palm-trees and grapes, and thou cause forth- gushing rivers to gush forth in its midst;

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 95
records.text: Or thou make the heaven to fall on us, as thou hast given out, in pieces; or thou bring God and the angels to vouch for thee;

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 96
records.text: Or thou have a house of gold; or thou mount up into Heaven; nor will we believe in thy mounting up, till thou send down to us a book which we may read." SAY: Praise be to my Lord! Am I more than a man, an apostle?

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 97
records.text: And what hindereth men from believing, when the guidance hath come to them, but that they say, "Hath God sent a man as an apostle?"

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 98
records.text: SAY: Did angels walk the earth as its familiars, we had surely sent them an angel-apostle out of Heaven.

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 99
records.text: SAY: God is witness enough between you and me. His servants He scanneth, eyeth.

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 100
records.text: And He whom God shall guide will be guided indeed; and whom he shall mislead thou shalt find none to assist, but Him: and we will gather them together on the day of the resurrection, on their faces, blind and dumb and deaf: Hell shall be their abode: so oft as its fires die down, we will rekindle the flame.

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 101
records.text: This shall be their reward for that they believed not our signs and said, "When we shall have become bones and dust, shall we surely be raised a new creation?"

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 102
records.text: Do they not perceive that God, who created the Heavens and the Earth, is able to create their like? And he hath ordained them a term; there is no doubt of it: but the wicked refuse everything except unbelief.

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 103
records.text: SAY: If ye held the treasures of my Lord's mercy ye would certainly refrain from them through fear of spending them: for man is covetous.

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 104
records.text: We therefore gave to Moses nine clear signs. Ask thou, therefore, the children of Israel how it was when he came unto them, and Pharaoh said to him, "Verily, I deem thee, O Moses, a man enchanted."

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 105
records.text: Said Moses, "Thou knowest that none hath sent down these clear signs but the Lord of the Heavens and of the Earth; and I surely deem thee, O Pharaoh, a person lost."

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 106
records.text: So Pharaoh sought to drive them out of the land; but we drowned him and all his followers.

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 107
records.text: And after his death, we said to the children of Israel, "Dwell ye in the land:" and when the promise of the next life shall come to pass, we will bring you both up together to judgment. In truth have we sent down the Koran, and in truth hath it descended, and we have only sent thee to announce and to warn.

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 108
records.text: And we have parcelled out the Koran into sections, that thou mightest recite it unto men by slow degrees, and we have sent it down piecemeal.

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 109
records.text: SAY: Believe ye therein or believe ye not? They verily to whom knowledge had been given previously, fall on their faces worshipping when it is recited to them, and say: "Glory be to God! the promise of our Lord is made good!"

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 110
records.text: They fall down on their faces weeping, and It increaseth their humility.

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 111
records.text: SAY: Call upon God (Allah),28 or call upon the God of Mercy (Arrahman), by whichsoever ye will invoke him: He hath most excellent names. And be not loud in thy prayer, neither pronounce it too low;29 but between these follow a middle way:

records.label: Surah 17 · edition paragraph 112
records.text: And SAY: Praise be to God who hath not begotten a son, who hath no partner in the Kingdom, nor any protector on account of weakness. And magnify him by proclaiming His greatness.30

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 1
records.text: In the Name of God, the Compassionate, the Merciful

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 2
records.text: PRAISE be to God, who hath sent down the Book to his servant, and hath not made it tortuous1

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 3
records.text: But direct; that it may warn of a grievous woe from him, and announce to the faithful who do the things that are right, that a goodly reward, wherein they shall abide for ever, awaiteth them;

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 4
records.text: And that it may warn those who say, "God hath begotten a Son."

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 5
records.text: No knowledge of this have either they or their fathers! A grievous saying to come out of their mouths! They speak no other than a lie!

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 6
records.text: And haply, if they believe not in this new revelation, thou wilt slay thyself, on their very footsteps, out of vexation.

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 7
records.text: Verily, we have made all that is on earth as its adornment, that we might make trial who among mankind would excel in works:

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 8
records.text: But we are surely about to reduce all that is thereon to dust!

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 9
records.text: Hast thou reflected that the Inmates of THE CAVE and of Al Rakim2 were on our wondrous signs?

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 10
records.text: When the youths betook them to the cave they said, "O our Lord! grant us mercy from before thee, and order for us our affair aright."

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 11
records.text: Then struck we upon their ears with deafness in the cave for many a year:

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 12
records.text: Then we awaked them that we might know which of the two parties could best reckon the space of their abiding.

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 13
records.text: We will relate to thee their tale with truth. They were youths who had believed in their Lord, and in guidance had we increased them;

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 14
records.text: And we had made them stout of heart, when they stood up and said, "Our Lord is Lord of the Heavens and of the Earth: we will call on no other God than Him; for in that case we had said a thing outrageous.

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 15
records.text: These our people have taken other gods beside Him, though they bring no clear proof for them; but, who more iniquitous than he who forgeth a lie of God?

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 16
records.text: So when ye shall have separated you from them and from that which they worship beside God, then betake you to the cave: Your Lord will unfold his mercy to you, and will order your affairs for you for the best."

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 17
records.text: And thou mightest have seen the sun when it arose, pass on the right of their cave, and when it set, leave them on the left, while they were in its spacious chamber. This is one of the signs of God. Guided indeed is he whom God guideth; but for him whom He misleadeth, thou shalt by no means find a patron, director.

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 18
records.text: And thou wouldst have deemed them awake,3 though they were sleeping: and we turned them to the right and to the left. And in the entry lay their dog with paws outstretched.4 Hadst thou come suddenly upon them, thou wouldst surely have turned thy back on them in flight, and have been filled with fear at them.

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 19
records.text: So we awaked them that they might question one another. Said one of them, "How long have ye tarried here?" They said, "We have tarried a day or part of day." They said, "Your Lord knoweth best how long ye have tarried: Send now one of you with this your coin into the city, and let him mark who therein hath purest food, and from him let him bring you a supply: and let him be courteous, and not discover you to any one.

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 20
records.text: For they, if they find you out, will stone you or turn you back to their faith, and in that case it will fare ill with you for ever."

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 21
records.text: And thus made we their adventure known to their fellow citizens, that they might learn that the promise of God is true, and that as to "the Hour" there is no doubt of its coming. When they disputed among themselves concerning what had befallen them, some said, "Build a building over them; their Lord knoweth best about them." Those who prevailed in the matter said, "A place of worship will we surely raise over them."

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 22
records.text: Some say, "They were three; their dog the fourth:" others say, "Five; their dog the sixth," guessing at the secret: others say, "Seven; and their dog the eighth." SAY: My Lord best knoweth the number: none, save a few, shall know them.

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 23
records.text: Therefore be clear in they discussions about them,5 and ask not any Christian concerning them.

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 24
records.text: Say not thou of a thing, " I will surely do it to-morrow;" without , "If God will."6 And when thou hast forgotten, call thy Lord to mind; and say, "Haply my Lord will guide me, that I may come near to the truth of this story with correctness."

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 25
records.text: And they tarried in their cave 300 years, and 9 years over.7

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 26
records.text: SAY: God best knoweth how long they tarried: With Him are the secrets of the Heavens and of the Earth: Look thou and hearken unto Him alone.8 Man hath no guardian but Him, and none may bear part in his judgments:-

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 27
records.text: And publish what hath been revealed to thee of the Book of thy Lord-none may change his words,-and thou shalt find no refuge beside Him.

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 28
records.text: Be patient with those who call upon their Lord at morn and even, seeking his face: and let not thine eyes be turned away from them in quest of the pomp of this life;9 neither obey him10 whose heart we have made careless of the remembrance of Us, and who followeth his own lusts, and whose ways are unbridled.

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 29
records.text: And SAY: the truth is from your Lord: let him then who will, believe; and let him who will, be an infidel. But for the offenders we have got ready the fire whose smoke shall enwrap them: and if they implore help, helped shall they be with water like molten brass which shall scald their Wretched the drink! and an unhappy couch!

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 30
records.text: But as to those who have believed and done the things that are right,-Verily we will not suffer the reward of him whose works were good, to perish!

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 31
records.text: For them, the gardens of Eden, under whose shades shall rivers flow: decked shall they be therein with bracelets of gold, and green robes of silk and rich brocade shall they wear, reclining them therein on thrones. Blissful the reward! and a pleasant couch!11

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 32
records.text: And set forth to them as a parable two men; on one of whom we bestowed two gardens of grape vines, and surrounded both with palm trees, and placed corn fields between them: Each of the gardens did yield its fruit, and failed not thereof at all:

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 33
records.text: And we caused a river to flow in their midst: And this man received his fruit, and said, disputing with him, to his companion, "More have I than thou of wealth, and my family is mightier."

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 34
records.text: And he went into his garden-to his own soul unjust. He said, "I do not think that this will ever perish:

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 35
records.text: And I do not think that 'the Hour' will come: and even if I be taken back to my Lord, I shall surely find a better than it in exchange."

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 36
records.text: His fellow said to him, disputing with him, "What ! hast thou no belief in him who created thee of the dust, then of the germs of life,12 then fashioned thee a perfect man?

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 37
records.text: But God is my Lord; and no other being will I associate with my Lord.

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 38
records.text: And why didst thou not say when thou enteredst thy garden, 'What God willeth! There is no power but in God.' Though thou seest that I have less than thou of wealth and children,

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 39
records.text: Yet haply my Lord may bestow on me better than thy garden, and may send his bolts upon it out of Heaven, so that the next dawn shall find it barren dust;

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 40
records.text: Or its water become deep sunk, so that thou art unable to find it."

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 41
records.text: And his fruits were encompassed by destruction. Then began he to turn down the palms of his hands at what he had spent on it; for its vines were falling down on their trellises, and he said, "Oh that I had not joined any other god to my Lord!"

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 42
records.text: And he had no host to help him instead of God, neither was he able to help himself.

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 43
records.text: Protection in such a case is of God-the Truth: He is the best rewarder, and He bringeth to the best issue.

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 44
records.text: And set before them a similitude of the present life. It is as water which we send down from Heaven, and the herb of the Earth is mingled with it, and on the morrow it becometh dry stubble which the winds scatter: for God hath power over all things.

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 45
records.text: Wealth and children are the adornment of this present life: but good works, which are lasting, are better in the sight of thy Lord as to recompense, and better as to hope.

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 46
records.text: And call to mind the day when we will cause the mountains to pass away,13 and thou shalt see the earth a levelled plain, and we will gather mankind together, and not leave of them any one.

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 47
records.text: And they shall be set before thy Lord in ranks:-"Now are ye come unto us as we created you at first: but ye thought that we should not make good to you the promise."

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 48
records.text: And each shall have his book put into his hand: and thou shalt see the wicked in alarm at that which is therein: and they shall say, "O woe to us! what meaneth this Book? It leaveth neither small nor great unnoted down!" And they shall find all that they have wrought present to them, and thy Lord will not deal unjustly with any one.

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 49
records.text: When we said to the angels, "Prostrate yourselves before Adam," they all prostrated them save Eblis, who was of the Djinn,14 and revolted from his Lord's behest. behest.-What! will ye then take him and his offspring as patrons rather than Me? and they your enemies? Sad exchange for the ungodly!

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 50
records.text: I made them not witnesses of the creation of the Heavens and of the Earth, nor of their own creation, neither did I take seducers as my helpers.

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 51
records.text: On a certain day, God shall say, "Call ye on the companions ye joined with me, deeming them to be gods:" and they shall call on them, but they shall not answer them: then will we place a valley of perdition between them:

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 52
records.text: And the wicked shall see the fire, and shall have a foreboding that they shall be flung into it, and they shall find no escape from it.

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 53
records.text: And now in this Koran we have presented to man similitudes of every kind: but, at most things is man a caviller.

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 54
records.text: And what, now that guidance is come to them, letteth men from believing and from asking forgiveness of their Lord-unless they wait till that the doom of the ancients overtake them, or the chastisement come upon them in the sight of the universe?

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 55
records.text: We send not our Sent Ones but to announce and to warn: but the infidels cavil with vain words in order to refute the truth; and they treat my signs and their own warnings with scorn.

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 56
records.text: But who is worse than he who when told of the signs of his Lord turneth him away and forgetteth what in time past his hands have wrought? Truly we have thrown veils over their hearts lest they should understand this Koran, and into their ears a heaviness:

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 57
records.text: And if thou bid them to "the guidance" yet will they not even then be guided ever.

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 58
records.text: The gracious one, full of compassion, is thy Lord! if he would have chastised them for their demerits he would have hastened their chastisement. But they have a time fixed for the accomplishment of our menaces: and beside God they shall find no refuge.

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 59
records.text: And those cities did we destroy when they became impious; and of their coming destruction we gave them warning.

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 60
records.text: Remember when Moses said to his servant, "I will not stop till I reach the confluence of the two seas,15 or for years will I journey on."

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 61
records.text: But when they reached their confluence, they forgot their fish, and it took its way in the sea at will.

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 62
records.text: And when they had passed on, said Moses to his servant, "Bring us our morning meal; for now have we incurred weariness from this journey."

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 63
records.text: He said, "What thinkest thou? When we repaired to the rock for rest I forgot the fish; and none but Satan made me forget it, so as not to mention it; and it hath taken its way in the sea in a wondrous sort."

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 64
records.text: He said, "It is this we were in quest of."16 And they both went back retracing their footsteps.

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 65
records.text: Then found they one of our servants to whom we had vouchsafed our mercy, and whom we had instructed with our knowledge.

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 66
records.text: And Moses said to him, "Shall I follow thee that thou teach me, for guidance, of that which thou too hast been taught?"

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 67
records.text: He said, "Verily, thou canst not have patience with me;

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 68
records.text: How canst thou be patient in matters whose meaning thou comprehendest not?"

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 69
records.text: He said, "Thou shalt find me patient if God please, nor will I disobey thy bidding."

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 70
records.text: He said, "Then, if thou follow me, ask me not of aught until I have given thee an account thereof."

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 71
records.text: So they both went on, till they embarked in a ship, and he-the unknown-staved it in. "What!" said Moses, "hast thou staved it in that thou mayest drown its crew? a strange thing now hast thou done!"

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 72
records.text: He said, "Did I not tell thee that thou couldst not have patience with me?"

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 73
records.text: He said, "Chide me not that I forgat, nor lay on me a hard command."

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 74
records.text: Then went they on till they met a youth, and he slew him. Said Moses, "Hast thou slain him who is free from guilt of blood? Now hast thou wrought a grievous thing!"

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 75
records.text: He said, "Did I not tell thee that thou couldst not have patience with me?"

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 76
records.text: Moses said, "If after this I ask thee aught, then let me be thy comrade no longer; but now hast thou my excuse."

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 77
records.text: They went on till they came to the people of a city. Of this people they asked food, but they refused them for guests. And they found in it a wall that was about to fall, and he set it upright. Said Moses, "If thou hadst wished, for this thou mightest have obtained pay."

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 78
records.text: He said, "This is the parting point between me and thee. But I will first tell thee the meaning of that which thou couldst not await with patience.

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 79
records.text: "As to the vessel, it belonged to poor men who toiled upon the sea, and I was minded to damage it, for in their rear was a king who seized every ship by force.

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 80
records.text: As to the youth his parents were believers, and we feared lest he should trouble them by error and infidelity.

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 81
records.text: And we desired that their Lord might give them in his place a child, better than he in virtue, and nearer to filial piety.

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 82
records.text: And as to the wall, it belonged to two orphan youths in the city, and beneath it was their treasure: and their father was a righteous man: and thy Lord desired that they should reach the age of strength, and take forth their treasure through the mercy of thy Lord. And not of mine own will have I done this. This is the interpretation of that which thou couldst not bear with patience."

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 83
records.text: They will ask thee of Dhoulkarnain [the two-horned17]. SAY: I will recite to you an account of him.

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 84
records.text: We stablished his power upon the earth, and made for him a way to everything. And a route he followed,

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 85
records.text: Until when he reached the setting of the sun, he found it to set in a miry fount; and hard by he found a people.

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 86
records.text: We said, "O Dhoulkarnain! either chastise or treat them generously."

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 87
records.text: "The impious," said he, "will we surely chastise;" then shall he be taken back to his Lord, and he will chastise him with a grievous chastisement.

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 88
records.text: But as to him who believeth and doeth that which is right, he shall have a generous recompense, and we will lay on them our easy behests.

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 89
records.text: Then followed he a route,

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 90
records.text: Until when he reached the rising of the sun he found it to rise on a people to whom we had given no shelter from it.

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 91
records.text: Thus it was. And we had full knowledge of the forces that were with him.

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 92
records.text: Then followed he a route

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 93
records.text: Until he came between the two mountains, beneath which he found a people who scarce understood a language.

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 94
records.text: They said, "O Dhoulkarnain! verily, Gog and Magog18 waste this land; shall we then pay thee tribute, so thou build a rampart19 between us and them?"

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 95
records.text: He said, "Better than your tribute is the might wherewith my Lord hath strengthened me; but help me strenuously, and I will set a barrier between you and them.

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 96
records.text: Bring me blocks of iron,"-until when it filled the space between the mountain sides-"Ply," said he, "your bellows,"-until when he had made it red with heat (fire), he said,-"Bring me molten brass that I may pour upon it."

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 97
records.text: And Gog and Magog were not able to scale it, neither were they able to dig through it.

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 98
records.text: "This," said he, "is a mercy from my Lord:

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 99
records.text: But when the promise of my Lord shall come to pass, he will turn it to dust; and the promise of my Lord is true."

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 100
records.text: On that day we will let them dash like billows one over another; and there shall be a blast on the trumpet, and we will gather them together in a body.

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 101
records.text: And we will set Hell on that day close before the infidels,

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 102
records.text: Whose eyes were veiled from my warning, and who had no power to hear.

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 103
records.text: What! do the infidels think that they can take my servants as their patrons, beside Me? Verily, we have got Hell ready as the abode of the infidels.

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 104
records.text: SAY: Shall we tell you who they are that have lost their labour most?

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 105
records.text: Whose aim in the present life hath been mistaken, and who deem that what they do is right?

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 106
records.text: They are those who believe not in the signs of the Lord, or that they shall ever meet him. Vain, therefore, are their works; and no weight will we allow them on the day of resurrection.

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 107
records.text: This shall be their reward-Hell.20 Because they were unbelievers, and treated my signs and my Apostles with scorn.

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 108
records.text: But as for those who believe and do the things that are right, they shall have the gardens of Paradise21 for their abode:

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 109
records.text: They shall remain therein for ever: they shall wish for no change from it.

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 110
records.text: SAY: Should the sea become ink, to write the words of my Lord, the sea would surely fail ere the words of my Lord would fail, though we brought its like in aid.

records.label: Surah 18 · edition paragraph 111
records.text: SAY: In sooth I am only a man like you. It hath been revealed to me that your God is one only God: let him then who hopeth to meet his Lord work a righteous work: nor let him give any other creature a share in the worship of his Lord.

records.label: Surah 19 · edition paragraph 1
records.text: In the Name of God, the Compassionate, the Merciful

records.label: Surah 19 · edition paragraph 2
records.text: KAF. HA. YA. AIN. SAD.2 A recital of thy Lord's mercy to his servant Zachariah;

records.label: Surah 19 · edition paragraph 3
records.text: When he called upon his Lord with secret calling,

records.label: Surah 19 · edition paragraph 4
records.text: And said: "O Lord, verily my bones are weakened, and the hoar hairs glisten on my head,

records.label: Surah 19 · edition paragraph 5
records.text: And never, Lord, have I prayed to thee with ill success.

records.label: Surah 19 · edition paragraph 6
records.text: But now I have fears for my kindred after me;3 and my wife is barren:

records.label: Surah 19 · edition paragraph 7
records.text: Give me, then, a successor as thy special gift, who shall be my heir and an heir of the family of Jacob: and make him, Lord, well pleasing to thee."

records.label: Surah 19 · edition paragraph 8
records.text: -"O Zachariah! verily we announce to thee a son,-his name John:

records.label: Surah 19 · edition paragraph 9
records.text: That name We have given to none before him."4

records.label: Surah 19 · edition paragraph 10
records.text: He said: "O my Lord! how when my wife is barren shall I have a son, and when I have now reached old age, failing in my powers?"

records.label: Surah 19 · edition paragraph 11
records.text: He said: So shall it be. Thy Lord hath said, Easy is this to me, for I created thee aforetime when thou wast nothing."

records.label: Surah 19 · edition paragraph 12
records.text: He said: "Vouchsafe me, O my Lord! a sign." He said: "Thy sign shall be that for three nights, though sound in health, thou speakest not to man."

records.label: Surah 19 · edition paragraph 13
records.text: And he came forth from the sanctuary to his people, and made signs to them to sing praises morn and even.

records.label: Surah 19 · edition paragraph 14
records.text: We said: "O John! receive the Book with purpose of heart:"5-and We bestowed on him wisdom while yet a child;

records.label: Surah 19 · edition paragraph 15
records.text: And mercifulness from Ourself, and purity; and pious was he, and duteous to his parents; and not proud, rebellious.

records.label: Surah 19 · edition paragraph 16
records.text: And peace was on him on the day he was born, and the day of his death, and shall be on the day when he shall be raised to life!

records.label: Surah 19 · edition paragraph 17
records.text: And make mention in the Book, of Mary, when she went apart from her family, eastward,6

records.label: Surah 19 · edition paragraph 18
records.text: And took a veil to shroud herself from them:7 and we sent our spirit8 to her, and he took before her the form of a perfect man.9

records.label: Surah 19 · edition paragraph 19
records.text: She said: "I fly for refuge from thee to the God of Mercy! If thou fearest Him, begone from me."

records.label: Surah 19 · edition paragraph 20
records.text: He said: "I am only a messenger of thy Lord, that I may bestow on thee a holy son."

records.label: Surah 19 · edition paragraph 21
records.text: She said: "How shall I have a son, when man hath never touched me? and I am not unchaste."

records.label: Surah 19 · edition paragraph 22
records.text: He said: "So shall it be. Thy Lord hath said: 'Easy is this with me;' and we will make him a sign to mankind, and a mercy from us. For it is a thing decreed."

records.label: Surah 19 · edition paragraph 23
records.text: And she conceived him,10 and retired with him to a far-off place.

records.label: Surah 19 · edition paragraph 24
records.text: And the throes came upon her11 by the trunk of a palm. She said: "Oh, would that I had died ere this, and been a thing forgotten, forgotten quite!"

records.label: Surah 19 · edition paragraph 25
records.text: And one cried to her from below her:12 "Grieve not thou, thy Lord hath provided a streamlet at thy feet:-

records.label: Surah 19 · edition paragraph 26
records.text: And shake the trunk of the palm-tree toward thee:13 it will drop fresh ripe dates upon thee.

records.label: Surah 19 · edition paragraph 27
records.text: Eat then and drink, and be of cheerful eye:14 and shouldst thou see a man,

records.label: Surah 19 · edition paragraph 28
records.text: Say,-Verily, I have vowed abstinence to the God of mercy.-To no one will I speak this day."

records.label: Surah 19 · edition paragraph 29
records.text: Then came she with the babe to her people, bearing him. They said, "O Mary! now hast thou done a strange thing!

records.label: Surah 19 · edition paragraph 30
records.text: O sister of Aaron!15 Thy father was not a man of wickedness, nor unchaste thy mother."

records.label: Surah 19 · edition paragraph 31
records.text: And she made a sign to them, pointing towards the babe. They said, "How shall we speak with him who is in the cradle, an infant?"

records.label: Surah 19 · edition paragraph 32
records.text: It said,16 "Verily, I am the servant of God; He hath given me the Book, and He hath made me a prophet;

records.label: Surah 19 · edition paragraph 33
records.text: And He hath made me blessed wherever I may be, and hath enjoined me prayer and almsgiving so long as I shall live;

records.label: Surah 19 · edition paragraph 34
records.text: And to be duteous to her that bare me: and he hath not made me proud, depraved.

records.label: Surah 19 · edition paragraph 35
records.text: And the peace of God was on me the day I was born, and will be the day I shall die, and the day I shall be raised to life."

records.label: Surah 19 · edition paragraph 36
records.text: This is Jesus, the son of Mary; this is a statement of the truth concerning which they doubt.

records.label: Surah 19 · edition paragraph 37
records.text: It beseemeth not God to beget a son. Glory be to Him! when he decreeth a thing, He only saith to it, Be, and it Is.17

records.label: Surah 19 · edition paragraph 38
records.text: And verily, God is my Lord and your Lord; adore Him then. This is the right way.

records.label: Surah 19 · edition paragraph 39
records.text: But the Sects have fallen to variance among themselves about Jesus: but woe, because of the assembly of a great day, to those who believe not!

records.label: Surah 19 · edition paragraph 40
records.text: Make them hear, make them behold the day when they shall come before us! But the offenders this day are in a manifest error.

records.label: Surah 19 · edition paragraph 41
records.text: Warn them of the day of sighing when the decree shall be accomplished, while they are sunk in heedlessness and while they believe not.

records.label: Surah 19 · edition paragraph 42
records.text: Verily, we will inherit the earth and all who are upon it. To us shall they be brought back.

records.label: Surah 19 · edition paragraph 43
records.text: Make mention also in the Book of Abraham; for he was a man of truth, a Prophet.18
